docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Briefs and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Briefs and format (trap): 14-point type, double spaced; L.R. 7.1(d)(3) page limits and L.R. 5.1(a) format are enforced, and oversized briefs need a motion giving specific reasons. A brief plus exhibits over 12 pages needs a table of contents, table of authorities, and index (the Phase I order requires a table of contents, index of authorities, and index of exhibits in all briefs, with tabbed exhibits and relevant portions highlighted). Cite the record as “ECF No. 1-2, PageID.1234,” and cite an opponent’s statement by docket and page. Use the latest Bluebook. No counsel listings or other state-court-style matter in captions; such filings will not be docketed. Each motion needs a separate brief; never embed a motion in a response, reply, or another motion’s text or footnotes. Concurrence under L.R. 7.1(a) is strictly enforced, with costs for noncomplianc

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment (trap): One summary judgment motion per party without leave. The page says the motion must begin with a “Statement of Material Facts,” which counts against the brief’s page limit, with page-and-line record citations and full-text sources filed as tabbed, indexed exhibits; the response begins with a “Counterstatement of Material Facts” explaining each dispute with record cites. The Phase I order (December 2022) frames it as numbered paragraphs answered paragraph by paragraph, with uncontroverted facts deemed admitted. Skip boilerplate standards and string cites. The page says to submit copies of unpublished opinions, while the Phase I order says to link citations and not attach cases (but also that unpublished cases should be attached).

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Discovery disputes (trap): The page’s protocol: (1) meet and confer in person (email is not enough); (2) email the paralegal to request an in-person status conference in Flint, with a dispute summary and certification of step 1, and file a joint letter through CM/ECF Utilities at least 5 business days before (or the conference is canceled); (3) only then move, attaching the full requests and responses and any full deposition transcript. If argument is set, file a joint statement of unresolved issues 48 hours before. The Phase I order instead makes a blanket referral of discovery to the magistrate judge; consult that chambers’ procedures first. Discovery must be served early enough for responses before the cutoff, and all discovery motions must be filed before the cutoff. Extensions that affect other dates or lack good cause are not permitted.

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Sealing (trap): File a motion for leave before docketing anything under seal, after seeking concurrence, showing compelling reasons with detailed analysis under Shane Group. If the motion itself reveals nothing sensitive, e-file it publicly with the items to be sealed as separately docketed sealed exhibits. If the motion itself is sensitive, or the material must be kept from opposing counsel, send the motion and items as separate Word files through CM/ECF Utilities to the case manager and do not e-file anything. Requests to seal whole briefs or all exhibits for limited sensitive content will usually be denied.

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Stipulations, proposed orders, and contact
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Stipulations, proposed orders, and contact: Every stipulation needs a proposed order; submit both in Word through CM/ECF Utilities, not e-filed, and never on party or firm letterhead. A non-e-filing pro se party must sign the stipulation in ink. No ex parte communications. Contact the case manager or paralegal on procedural and scheduling matters only; contacting law clerks is discouraged. Notify chambers by email within 1 business day of a settlement or a resolved motion, and file a notice withdrawing the motion.

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling conference
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling conference: Notice issues 2 to 4 weeks after the answer (after all defendants answer, if more than one); the posted notice sets a telephonic conference. Lead counsel must attend. The Rule 26(f) plan must use the court’s template, which tracks the Phase I order, with hard dates; plans with vague timeframes are rejected. The page sets the plan deadline at 5 business days before the conference; the posted notice says 7 days. Rule 26(a)(1) disclosures are generally due 14 days after the conference. Pro hac vice admission is not permitted, and L.R. 83.20(f) local counsel is strictly enforced. Social Security and pro se prisoner civil rights cases generally go to the magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — TROs and removal
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. TROs and removal: Even ex parte TROs require some notice to the opposing party and a chance to be heard unless good cause is shown; a conference usually precedes any TRO or preliminary injunction hearing. Email the case manager and judicial assistant on filing. Motions to remand for procedural defects are due within 30 days of removal; oral argument is typically held on remand motions.

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Settlement and final pretrial
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Settlement and final pretrial: Settlement conference: parties, trial attorneys, and insurers with full authority must attend, ready for serious discussion; sanctions if the person with full authority fails to appear. Joint requests for state case evaluation or outside mediation are usually granted after discovery. The trial date is set after ADR or dispositive motions, whichever is later, in consultation with counsel, so adjournments are rarely granted. The joint final pretrial order is filed through CM/ECF and must strictly follow L.R. 16.2; foundation or authenticity objections not raised before trial are waived. Final pretrial attendance by trial counsel, natural-person parties, a representative with full authority, and any controlling insurer is required in person; phone availability is allowed only with prior court permission, generally given only

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Exhibits: plaintiff (or government) numbers, defendant letters; make all exhibits available for inspection 1 week before the final pretrial conference, with exhibit lists to chambers by the deadline set there. Authentication of inspected exhibits is deemed established unless contested by notice at or before that conference. Disclose computer-generated evidence and data 1 week before trial. Stipulated jury instructions, one per page with authority, double spaced, plus each party’s disputed instructions, go directly to chambers in Word (on USB per the page). The court gives its own introductory and concluding instructions and charges the jury before closing. The court conducts general voir dire but counsel may question jurors; contentious questions are due in writing 3 days before voir dire. Raise mid-trial evidentiary issues before or after the t

docs.t: Judge Shalina D. Kumar (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shalina D. Kumar, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases (trap): Counsel must meet within 10 days of arraignment, or the government files the 03-AO-027 Discovery Notice. Pretrial motions are due 20 days after arraignment; date changes need a motion with a stipulation and Speedy Trial Act waiver if the trial date moves. The defendant must attend all hearings unless excused, and writs must be submitted 4 weeks before the court date. Witness lists, proposed voir dire, a joint case summary, joint jury instructions, verdict form, and trial briefs go through CM/ECF Utilities by the scheduling order deadline. Foundation, chain-of-custody, and scientific-analysis challenges are due at or before the final pretrial conference with an item-by-item good-faith basis (the order gives 7 days before trial for scientific analysis). Use yellow and blue exhibit stickers; witnesses, including law enforcement, tes

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Contact with chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Contact with chambers (trap): Staff will not advise anyone on motion practice (whether, what, how, or when to file); callers are referred to the rules and these guidelines. In the rare case you must call or email the court, include opposing counsel. Do not ask about the status of pending motions, and do not call to confirm a scheduling conference: unless canceled on the docket, it goes forward.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Motions (trap): Seek concurrence on every motion by speaking with opposing counsel in person or by phone, preferably before drafting, and more than pro forma. Failure to seek concurrence or follow L.R. 7.1(a) may get the motion struck. Briefs must be in searchable text, and exhibits filed with the CM/ECF exhibit feature, or the motion may be struck. If a brief and its exhibits exceed 12 pages in total, include a table of contents, a table of authorities, and an index of exhibits. References to briefs, filings, or another party’s argument must cite the docket number and the “PgID” number.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Hearings and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Hearings and courtesy copies: Motions are typically decided on the briefs without a hearing. Hearing continuances are granted only on motion for good cause. No courtesy copies; the judge prefers that none be submitted.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Appearances and conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Appearances and conduct (trap): Pro hac vice admission is not permitted (L.R. 83.20(c)), and waivers are highly disfavored. Telephonic appearances are very rarely allowed and never at scheduling conferences. Business attire in court and on video. Stand when addressing the court, jury, or witnesses and when the jury enters or leaves; ask before approaching the bench, witnesses, or jury, and don’t touch the bench, stand, or jury box. The courtroom has no public WiFi; counsel table offers HDMI, VGA, and 3.5mm audio inputs, and no devices, cords, or adapters are provided. You may arrange a visit to test the equipment.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling and discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling and discovery (trap): The court orders a joint discovery plan on its template and sets a scheduling conference, likely by Zoom. Early discovery by agreement is encouraged. The discovery period is strictly enforced; in rare cases one extension is allowed on a detailed showing of good cause, requested no later than 1 week before discovery closes. Consider contacting the court for informal resolution before filing a discovery motion. Discovery motions generally go to a discovery master or magistrate judge, and parties acting in bad faith bear the master’s costs.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Stipulated orders
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Stipulated orders: Stipulations are encouraged for routine matters such as filing extensions. Submit them in Word or WordPerfect through CM/ECF Utilities > Proposed Orders > Submit Proposed Order; noncompliant stipulations may be summarily struck. Allow 1–2 days for entry.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Jurisdiction, TROs, and ADR
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Jurisdiction, TROs, and ADR: Subject-matter jurisdiction is reviewed in every case; unclear jurisdictional grounds bring an order to show cause why the case should not be dismissed or remanded. Ex parte TRO requests are rarely considered; confer before any preliminary injunction hearing. The court may refer cases to a private mediator from its list (or one the parties jointly pick) or to a magistrate judge. If you mediate privately without a referral, tell the court the mediator’s name, contact information, and date in advance.

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Civil pretrial and trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Civil pretrial and trial (trap): The trial date is set in the initial scheduling order. Motions in limine are due at least 10 days before trial. Trial briefs are optional, due 5 days before trial, and may not contain new motions. Exchange exhibits and give the court a joint bench book of all exhibits, after conferring on admissibility. Joint proposed jury instructions are due before the final pretrial conference; any disagreements go in a single filing with agreed, plaintiff’s, and defendants’ instructions and responses. In bench trials, proposed findings and conclusions may be submitted before or during trial. Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., with a break around 11:00; counsel must be seated and ready by 8:30. One lawyer per side handles each advocacy function (an entire opening, each witness). Redirect is allowed only on good cause. Struck-jur

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases (trap): The government must immediately tell the court and defense counsel if any part of the case or investigation was opened in the U.S. Attorney’s Office before August 18, 2008; the judge may recuse. Comply with Local Criminal Rule 12.1 and L.R. 7.1(a) before any pretrial motion. No Rule 11(c)(1)(C) agreements; Rule 11(c)(1)(B) agreements and well-supported 5K1.1 departures are accepted. Negotiated pleas with sentencing restrictions, significant count reductions, or similar concessions are not ordinarily accepted after the final pretrial conference and plea cutoff. At the plea hearing, the AUSA should summarize the agreement in 120 seconds or less. Notices contesting foundation, chain of custody, or scientific analysis are due at least 7 days before trial; motions in limine at least 10 days before trial; proposed jury instruction

docs.t: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III (E.D. Mich.) — Pro se litigants
docs.x: Judge Stephen J. Murphy III, E.D. Mich.. Pro se litigants: Pro se litigants must follow the same rules and guidelines as attorneys. Letters to the court are not pleadings or motions and will be stricken.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): A courtesy copy of all dispositive motion papers (including responses, replies, and all exhibits) must go directly to chambers. For non-dispositive motions, a copy is required when the papers’ exhibits total more than 50 pages. Copies must show the .pdf header across the top, have exhibit tabs extending past the right edge, and be bound book-style along the left margin (comb, zip-band, or wire). Noncompliant copies are returned for reformatting before they are considered. Send the copy the same day you e-file; if it relates to a proceeding within the next 5 days or needs immediate attention, hand-deliver it to chambers by the morning of the next business day.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Motions and deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Motions and deadlines (trap): The clerk sends the hearing notice; dispositive motions are argued about 10 weeks after filing. No briefing schedule is issued, and L.R. 7.1(e) and Rule 6 response and reply deadlines are enforced even when the hearing is far off. Page extensions are not routinely granted. Extensions of time are not granted as a matter of course: explain specifically the unforeseen circumstances and propose a timetable for completing the task. Motions and responses need a separate brief; keep argument and factual summaries out of the motion itself. Never embed a motion in a response, reply, or another motion’s text or footnotes.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Briefing content
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Briefing content: Support the statement of material facts with record citations. Submit cited deposition pages plus the adjacent pages; if more than 5 pages are cited or the deposition is especially relevant, include the entire transcript. Underline or highlight specific references where applicable. Use well-chosen authority rather than boilerplate, and submit copies of cited unpublished or specialty-reporter opinions with the brief.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Discovery: Discovery may begin once the answer is received. It averages 3 to 4 months (6 to 12 months for complex or foreign discovery), and the court will honor a reasonable Rule 26(f) schedule. Serve discovery early enough to be answered and completed by the cutoff. Parties may stipulate to a short discovery extension only if no other case management date must move; submit the stipulation and order through CM/ECF Utilities (Proposed Order). Stipulated protective orders must comply with Rule 26(c) and may not pre-authorize sealed filings (sealing is governed by L.R. 5.3). Discovery motions are routinely referred to the magistrate judge; after referral, communicate only with that chambers.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling and status conferences
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling and status conferences: After the answer, the court requires the parties to submit, not file, a short statement of the case summarizing facts, legal basis, and proposed discovery; a Rule 26(f) discovery plan may be submitted instead. The scheduling order issues from these, with a conference only for unusual case management issues. Status conferences may be requested for good cause by letter and are often held by conference call.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — ADR and settlement
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. ADR and settlement: Facilitative mediation with an experienced facilitator is strongly encouraged, ideally after most discovery and before dispositive motions; it can be arranged without contacting chambers. Case evaluation under L.R. 16.3 requires a filed stipulation agreeing to be bound by all of Mich. Ct. R. 2.403, including sanctions, and must be completed before the final pretrial conference. A settlement conference is typically set before the close of discovery. Parties, trial attorneys, insurance representatives, and others needed to resolve the case must attend unless excused in advance for explained reasons.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial conference (trap): Generally 2 weeks before trial; pending motions in limine are heard the same day. Jury cases: proposed voir dire and joint jury instructions are due to chambers by close of business 1 week before the final pretrial conference, with instructions submitted through CM/ECF Utilities (Proposed Order). Bench trials: proposed findings, conclusions, and trial briefs through the same function on the same deadline.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Jury trials start on Tuesdays and run Monday through Friday, normally 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.; counsel must be in court by 8:15 a.m. The weekly schedule is set at the start of each trial week. In bench trials, provide two copies of exhibits to the court.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — TROs
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. TROs: Rule 65 governs. TROs without notice are rarely granted. Call the courtroom deputy when you file a TRO motion.

docs.t: Judge Thomas L. Ludington (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal sentencing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas L. Ludington, E.D. Mich.. Criminal sentencing (trap): On the day of a plea or verdict, defense counsel must arrange a probation interview within 7 days of conviction. The PSR is due within 56 days of conviction, and defense counsel must review it (and any addendum) with the defendant in person. PSR objections go to probation and opposing counsel, not the clerk, within 14 days of receipt, in a distinct document clearly marked as objections; improperly identified objections may be returned. Sentencing motions and memoranda are optional but must be filed at least 1 week before sentencing, with a copy to the probation officer. Habeas, Social Security, and prisoner civil rights cases generally go to the magistrate judge for a report and recommendation.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Informal matters and conferences
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Informal matters and conferences: No set time for informal matters (minor issues such as deadline changes or minor disputes). Notify opposing counsel, find out their availability, and call the judicial assistant to set an in-court or telephone conference. Most minor, agreed deadline changes can be handled by filing a motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents; the judge rules on these as soon as possible. For an emergency motion needing a formal hearing on the record, call chambers. After the Case Management Order is entered, counsel may call chambers to set a scheduling or status conference or a conference call about problems keeping the case from moving forward.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference (trap): Usually set after all defendants have answered or responded to the complaint; a party wanting it sooner must file a motion. Conferences are in person, usually in chambers (in the courtroom, on the record, when a party is pro se). Out-of-town counsel may participate by conference call but must give chambers contact information at least one business day before. Do not send an unprepared substitute or a lawyer who cannot commit on trial counsel’s calendar; be ready to discuss the facts, the Rule 16 Order’s topics, and settlement.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Before any discovery motion, the moving party must actually speak to opposing counsel, in person or by telephone, and certify the attempt in the motion; motions without the certification are denied without prejudice. If opposing counsel won’t return calls, detail those efforts in the certification. The judge either sets a hearing or rules on the papers. To request a hearing, say so in the motion or memorandum and call chambers once briefing is complete. For emergencies, call chambers for a preliminary telephone conference.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Expert disclosures (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Expert disclosures (trap): Non-retained experts (such as treating physicians and employees whose duties don’t regularly involve expert testimony) must be identified and given a Rule 26(a)(2)(C) summary of opinions and supporting facts, on the same date as the party’s other expert disclosures unless the CMO says otherwise. Undisclosed opinions may be excluded, and objections to sufficiency must be made promptly. Be ready at the Rule 16 conference to discuss expected expert types and the timing of reports and depositions; absent a stipulation, Rule 26 applies.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Most civil cases are referred to mediation; be ready to discuss timing at the Rule 16 conference and consider what discovery is needed for a meaningful mediation. Once referred, ADR deadlines are binding and may be extended only by court order.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Trial setting and final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Trial setting and final pretrial conference: Most cases are set on a firm three-week trial docket; assume your case is #1 unless told otherwise. St. Louis juries are picked at 9:00 a.m. or 1:15 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays. If the case is still on the docket two weeks before trial, chambers will call to set a final pretrial conference, normally two or three business days before trial; be ready to argue motions in limine there. For Cape Girardeau or Hannibal trials, the final pretrial conference is held in St. Louis unless you are told otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire and jury selection (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire and jury selection (trap): Before the case is called, supply an agreed, neutral brief statement of the case to read to the panel. Juror lists are not available in advance and must be returned to the clerk after selection. Attorneys usually conduct part of voir dire after the judge’s introductory questions; questions go to the panel as a whole first, with follow-ups to those who respond. No rapport-building questions, promises, speeches, argument, or talk about yourself. If the judge conducts all voir dire, proposed questions are due no later than two business days before trial. Challenges for cause are made outside the panel’s presence. Peremptories are exercised from the number to be seated plus total strikes, plaintiff first; in civil cases all remaining jurors deliberate and no alternates are designated.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Trial practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Trial practice (trap): Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; preliminary matters may not be raised at the start of the day but are heard 30 minutes before start, at lunch, or at day’s end. Examine from the lectern; no permission is needed to hand a witness an exhibit, but don’t hover over the witness or jury. No recross as of right: approach the bench and state the areas sought, which must be new matter from redirect. Exhibits in opening need opposing counsel’s consent and advance notice to the judge. Pre-mark exhibits (plaintiffs numbers, defendants letters; defendants with more than 78 exhibits should use a scheme like AA, AB … rather than AAAAA). Bring a list of exhibits received without objection, show each exhibit to opposing counsel before a witness, and show demonstratives in advance of trial. Before trial, tell opposing counsel which deposition po

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Jury instructions: Eighth Circuit Model Instructions for boilerplate and covered matters; Missouri Approved Instructions (or another state’s) for state-law issues. Meet and confer and, whenever possible, submit one joint package. Submit two complete sets: a clean set headed only “Instruction No. ___” and a set showing source, offering party, and numbers. Give the court a clean copy on disk at the final pretrial conference. Without agreement, expect the instruction conference in the evening after the trial day.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom technology and decorum
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom technology and decorum: The judge strongly encourages using the evidence camera (ELMO). Schedule training (usually 30 minutes or less) with the Case Management Team before trial; none on the day of trial. Confer with the Clerk’s office before using your own computer, and bring your own audio tape player. Stand when speaking and when the jury enters; address witnesses and counsel by last name with titles (never first names, even clients); no food, gum, drinks other than water, or cell phone use; no expressions to the jury from counsel table; young children only with an adult seated with them in the gallery.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Scheduling, informal matters, and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Scheduling, informal matters, and contact (trap): No regular informal matters docket. Most minor agreed deadline changes are handled by a written motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents. Telephone conferences on scheduling disputes are sometimes available; notify opposing counsel before seeking one. For an emergency needing a formal hearing on the record, call chambers to schedule it. In civil cases, do not email the judge or chambers staff unless specifically told to. In criminal cases, counsel may email the Judicial Assistant, Brian Crow (brian_crow@moed.uscourts.gov), about scheduling and logistics only, not substance.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Courtesy copies and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Courtesy copies and proposed orders: Courtesy copies of bulky summary judgment motions are helpful; no courtesy copies of other filings are needed. Any courtesy copy must show the ECF header (document number, page number, and filing date) on every page. File proposed orders in ECF as an exhibit to the motion, and also email them in Word format to Brian Crow.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Before any discovery motion, meet and confer and certify that you did. Exchanging “nasty letters or emails” does not count, and the judge does not want them attached to motions; counsel must actually talk. If the opponent won’t return calls, say so in the certification. The judge either sets discovery motions for hearing or rules on the papers. For an emergency discovery dispute, schedule a telephone conference on the record.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference and ADR
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference and ADR: Civil Rule 16 conferences are usually set after all defendants answer; a party wanting one sooner must file a motion. Follow the Order Setting Rule 16 Conference and the Case Management Order. Come prepared to discuss the facts, everything in the Rule 16 order (including settlement), and likely types of expert witnesses. Do not send an unprepared substitute attorney. Most civil cases are referred to mediation; be ready to discuss timing of the referral at the Rule 16 conference.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Experts (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Experts (trap): Absent stipulation or CMO provisions, Rule 26(a)(2) governs disclosure. Experts are limited to opinions and bases disclosed in discovery (report or deposition) and, absent unusual circumstances, may not supplement or change opinions after expert discovery closes; CMO deadlines override different deadlines in rules or statutes. Expert reports are hearsay and usually not admitted (impeachment use is allowed). Do not “tender the witness as an expert” or ask the judge to tell the jury a witness is an expert, and do not ask witnesses whether they consider themselves experts. Experts may not opine on the law or sum up the evidence.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Trial settings and final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Trial settings and final pretrial conference (trap): Most cases are set on a firm two-week trial docket mixing jury and non-jury, civil and criminal cases. Juries are picked at 9 a.m. and 1:15 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays in St. Louis. Unless told otherwise, assume you are #1 on the docket. Appear 30 minutes before scheduled jury selection for a final pretrial conference on evidentiary issues, motions in limine, and scheduling; an earlier, longer conference may be set or requested. In civil cases, exhibits not objected to in the pretrial submissions are received at the start of trial; bring a list of them. Order daily copy through the Case Management Team well in advance.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire: The jury panel list (names, municipality, employers, occupation, and spouse’s employer and occupation) is handed out as jurors enter; it is not provided in advance. Return all copies after selection. After the judge’s introductory questions, counsel may conduct part of voir dire. Ask general questions of the whole panel, then follow up with those who respond. No speeches, arguing the case, seeking promises, or questions just to hear jurors speak; submit in writing any questions you want the judge to ask. Cause challenges are made outside the panel’s presence; plaintiff then defense make peremptories. docs.t: Judge Stephen R. Clark (E.D. Mo.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephen R. Clark, E.D. Mo.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): Motions to seal not complying with Local Rule 13.05 are denied, generally without prejudice. A civil protective order contemplating sealed filings must require a motion for leave before any sealed filing (no automatic sealing) and set a date certain when the seal lifts or documents are removed. Orders that fail this or provide for continuing jurisdiction after the case ends will be denied.

docs.x: Judge Stephen R. Clark, E.D. Mo.. Criminal scheduling and continuances (trap): Request a change-of-plea hearing by emailing the paralegal with the agreed plea agreement attached. Any motion to continue a hearing or trial must state the length or proposed date and opposing counsel’s position on both. Sentencing continuance motions are due no later than 10 days before the hearing unless the grounds were unknowable then. Extensions for PSR objections must state

docs.t: Judge Stephen R. Clark (E.D. Mo.) — Emergencies and appearances
docs.x: Judge Stephen R. Clark, E.D. Mo.. Emergencies and appearances: For an emergency motion needing a hearing on the record, call chambers and follow up by email to the paralegal. Counsel must be admitted and file an entry of appearance (unless the Local Rules permit otherwise), or will not be allowed to participate.

docs.t: Judge Stephen R. Clark (E.D. Mo.) — ADR and settlement
docs.x: Judge Stephen R. Clark, E.D. Mo.. ADR and settlement: Civil cases (except habeas, social security, and bankruptcy appeals) are referred to ADR; multiple or partial-day sessions are encouraged. Plaintiff’s counsel is lead ADR counsel unless the parties notify the court in writing otherwise. A non-certified neutral requires a motion and special subject-matter expertise. ADR deadlines are binding; lead counsel must move to extend before they expire. On settlement, notify the court immediately; dismissal papers or a consent judgment are then due within 30 days.

docs.t: Judge Stephen R. Clark (E.D. Mo.) — Pretrial, trial, and courtroom
docs.x: Judge Stephen R. Clark, E.D. Mo.. Pretrial, trial, and courtroom: Be ready to argue motions in limine at the final pretrial conference. Electronic exhibit presentation is strongly encouraged; schedule training with the case management team before trial (none on trial day) and bring your own audio-tape device. Order daily transcripts from the court reporter at least two weeks before trial. Business-professional dress at all hearings and conferences (and on video). Laptops and tablets at counsel table are allowed, but audience use needs advance approval. On video, use a quiet, well-lit place, mute when not speaking, and don’t talk over others.

Motions for judicial notice or to declare an issue as a matter of law are entertained only if the parties contest the point; if it is uncontested, file a stipulation instead. Unopposed motions may be stricken unless good cause is shown for needing the court’s determination. Cite unpublished cases by Westlaw citation; if none is available, attach the case to the filing.

docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Motions in limine must concern specific evidence; motions asking that the parties be ordered to follow the Federal Rules of Evidence are discouraged. Raise objections to scientific and expert evidence by timely motion in limine, and Daubert issues by a Daubert motion under the scheduling-order deadline.

Parties are expected to attend a settlement conference midway through discovery. A request to continue it because discovery is incomplete will not be granted absent good cause.

The court intends to end the conference with the case ready for trial and prefers record-making at recesses or before or after the trial day. Civil trials are set on a trailing docket behind criminal cases; counsel learn their position at pretrial. docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, E.D. Okla.. Initial disclosures must be exchanged at least 1 business day before the conference. Begin discovery without waiting

docs.x: Judge Karen S. Marston, E.D. Pa.. docs.t: Judge Karen S. Marston (E.D. Pa.) — Continuances, injunctions, and arbitration
docs.x: Judge Karen S. Marston, E.D. Pa.. docs.t: Judge Karen S. Marston (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Karen S. Marston, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial and trial: The final pretrial conference is about 2 weeks before trial. One unified set of tailored jury instructions (Third Circuit models) and one verdict form; competing versions with explanations where disputed. File and email Word versions to Chambers_Judge_Marston@paed.uscourts.gov. Voir dire questions may be submitted 10 days before trial; the judge conducts individual voir dire at sidebar or in the jury room. Trial briefs 7 days before trial. Motions in limine: 5-page briefs, no more than 5 per party without leave. Joint exhibit book in hard copy and on a thu

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Meet and confer before any motion (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies and formatting (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Extensions and continuances (trap)

docs.t: Judge Kelley B. Hodge (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefs
docs.x: Judge Kelley B. Hodge, E.D. Pa.. Motions and briefs: Put all grounds in one comprehensive motion (e.g., a motion to dismiss shouldn’t be split by count). Request oral argument by letter or in the motion or response; the judge decides case by case and is most likely to hold it on dispositive motions.

Reply within 14 days, up to 10 pages; the non-movant may file an optional surreply within 7 days of the reply, up to 10 pages. A joint appendix of exhibits is encouraged; any appendix n

docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: The movant files a “Statement of Undisputed Facts” in numbered paragraphs with record references, preferably as a separate document. docs.x: Judge Michael Baylson, E.D. Pa.. Final pretrial conference: Held near the trial pool date, in court or by phone; all trial counsel must attend. Objections to authenticity, expert qualifications or admissibility, and FRE 701 lay opinion must be stated with particularity in the pretrial memorandum (L.R. 16.1(c)) or by motion. Requests for an offer of proof go to opposing counsel before trial, with a motion if unsatisfied. The court may impose time limits on a party’s case or on specific witnesses. Motions in limine may be filed after dispositive motions are decided or near the trial pool date; responses within 7 days.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and proposed orders: The preferred way to communicate is a formal written motion filed on ECF. docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Motion hearings and page limits
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Motion hearings and page limits: Non-dispositive motions are usually set for oral argument, with notice from the court. Telephonic motion hearings may be allowed when counsel’s offices are a significant distance from the court, unless the number of lawyers or the subject matter makes it impractical; request one through the judicial assistant. Follow Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits (cover sheet, tables, and certificate of service excluded). Requests to exceed are not routinely granted absent compelling reasons, and a noncompliant brief may be disregarded or the motion summarily denied.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): Serve written discovery early enough that responses are due before the deadline. Parties may agree to discovery after the deadline, but the court generally will not resolve disputes arising after it expires. Confer civilly and promptly; if that fails, bring the dispute promptly, preferably by motion specifying the relief sought. The discovery deadline is usually about 13 weeks before trial. Extensions for good cause are viewed favorably; otherwise deadlines are enforced.

docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Sealing and protective orders
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Sealing and protective orders: Confidentiality designations do not justify filing under seal; move for leave under the court’s Order Governing Sealing Confidential Information (filed at the start of each case), Local Rule 26.2, and ECF Rule 12.2. docs.t: Judge Christopher H. Steger (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling order deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Christopher H. Steger, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling order deadlines (trap): The form order counts back from trial: plaintiff’s expert disclosures 21 weeks, defendant’s 17 weeks; joinder and amendments 17 weeks; final witness lists 15 weeks; discovery (including evidence depositions) closes 13 weeks; Rule 26(a)(3)(A)(ii)–(iii) pretrial disclosures 9 weeks, with objections due 10 days after service; motions in limine, jury instructions, and verdict form 3 weeks; final pretrial conference 2 weeks. Filings before trial: At least 7 days before trial: file a final witness list limited to witnesses who will actually testify, a damages list (stipulated preferred), deposition designations and counter-designations, expert resumes, and briefs on contested legal issues, and jointly submit pre-marked exhibits numbered sequentially (plaintiff’s first, defendant’s continuing from plaintiff’s last number). Jury cases: file a single set of proposed stipulated jury instructions at least 10 days before trial. A disputed instruction goes under one heading with each side’s version and a one-paragraph statement with authority, and all instructions appear in sequence in one document; cite any model source. File a proposed joint verdict form (or competing forms with authority) at least 5 days before trial. Bench trials: file proposed findings of fact and conclusions o

docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: Trial starts at 9:00 a.m. in Courtroom 3A, Knoxville; if there are preliminary matters, notify chambers and be present at 8:30 a.m. Tell the courtroom deputy at least 2 days ahead if you will use the evidence presentation system. Exhibits must be submitted in electronic format for JERS; providing them to the courtroom deputy (preferably on USB, DVD, or CD) at least 7 days before trial is strongly encouraged. Move exhibits in individually, not collectively. Videotaped testimony must be pre-marked and made available to the other side. Question witnesses from the podium; only one lawyer per side may address a given witness. The court conducts general voir dire and counsel may supplement. Examination beyond redirect and recross is discouraged; no written Rule 50 motion is required. Jurors may take notes and take exhibits to the jury room. During delib

docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Mediation
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Mediation: Mediation is allowed and encouraged, and reasonable extensions of deadlines and trial dates to pursue it are granted. The form orders also require a joint report 22 weeks before trial on whether and when the case should be mediated (or why not).

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): Judge Crytzer will not consider any fact or argument not raised in the motion and supporting memorandum (with exhibits) or the response (with exhibits). That includes any separate “Statement of Undisputed Material Facts” or response to one, which may be struck, with any brief relying on it to be refiled (citing L.R. 7.1(a), (b), and (d) and the 25-page limit). Cross-motions for summary judgment should generally be briefed independently. Responses to dispositive motions are due in 21 days (L.R. 7.1(a)).

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and extensions (trap): Letters and emails (Crytzer_Chambers@tned.uscourts.gov) only for routine matters such as scheduling or settlement, and emergencies, never the merits; copy all counsel, and include all parties on calls where possible. Law clerks give no legal advice. To reset a hearing or extend a deadline, file a motion on the record; the court will not act on email requests absent emergency. A Rule 6(b) extension motion should state the standard with specific supporting facts, ask for a date certain or a set number of days, and say whether it is unopposed. The scheduling order changes only for good cause in strict compliance with Rule 6(b).

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Hearings and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Hearings and courtesy copies: All hearings are in person unless the court says otherwise or a party asks; Rule 16 and case management conferences may be by phone case by case. Final pretrial conferences, civil and criminal, are in person in Knoxville. Motions are usually decided without a hearing (L.R. 7.2), but a party may request one. If presenting evidence at a scheduled hearing, notify chambers in advance. No regular courtesy copies. If you must file at the last minute before a hearing or trial, promptly deliver a hard copy to chambers and bring one to court. For emergency motions, also email the motion and supporting papers to chambers, copying all counsel.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Page limits and sealing
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Page limits and sealing: Requests to exceed Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits are denied unless good cause is shown; noncompliant portions may be disregarded or the motion summarily denied. Also comply with Local Rule 5.1. Confidentiality designations do not justify sealing; move for leave under Rule 26(c) and Local Rule 26.2, consider whether only portions need sealing, and expect close scrutiny.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): Discovery generally runs about 6 months in a standard case and closes about 5.5 months before trial; serve written requests early enough that responses fall due before the deadline. Duplicative or overly burdensome discovery is not permitted. Before any motion to compel, meet and confer, then call the assigned magistrate judge’s chambers for a telephone conference. Only if the dispute survives that conference may you file a motion, which must certify compliance (plus the Rule 37(a)(1) certification if applicable).

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Experts and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Experts and Daubert (trap): Sample order: plaintiff’s experts about 8 months before trial, defendant’s about 7 months, rebuttal about 6.5 months. All objections to expert qualifications or testimony (F.R.E. 701–706 and Daubert) are due with dispositive motions, about 4 months before trial, or are waived; responses about 3 months before trial, and replies are not required. Motions to exclude expert testimony styled as motions in limine will not be entertained. If a Daubert motion is filed, file the challenged expert’s report at least 7 days before the Daubert hearing.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling order: motions and pretrial disclosures
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling order: motions and pretrial disclosures: Motions to amend or join parties about 29 weeks before trial; dispositive motions about 4 months before trial (untimely ones may be summarily denied). Motions in limine (non-expert) and other nondispositive motions about 60 days before trial; responses to motions in limine about 30 days before, and to other nondispositive motions 14 days after filing. Criminal motions in limine are due at least 15 days before trial unless otherwise set. 30 days before the final pretrial conference: final witness lists, exhibit lists, deposition designations, exhibit inspection, and damages lists; evidence depositions must be done. Written authenticity or admissibility objections are due 21 days before the conference or are waived. If the trial date moves, other dates not expressly tied to it stay. Civil trials

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial order and filings
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial order and filings: Plaintiff serves a draft pretrial order 45 days before the final pretrial conference (held about 2 weeks before trial); defendant responds within 5 business days. If no agreement, plaintiff notifies chambers at least 21 days before the conference; failure may mean dismissal. File the proposed order 5 days before the conference, including novel questions of law or evidence and trial length in 8-hour days. At least 7 days before trial: final witness list, damages list, deposition designations, expert resumes, briefs on contested legal issues, proposed findings and conclusions (bench issues), and jointly submitted pre-marked exhibits (plaintiff numbered 1, 2, 3; defendant lettered A, B, C; multiple parties identified on each). Electronic exhibits for JERS are strongly encouraged to the courtroom deputy by then, preferabl

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: The judge conducts preliminary voir dire and usually allows counsel to follow up; peremptory challenges go on a form. Opening time limits are set at the final pretrial conference; closing limits during trial. Stand and examine from the lectern; one attorney per witness, including objections. Keep sidebars to a minimum and raise issues at breaks. Give the courtroom deputy advance notice of video testimony, and at least 2 days’ notice to use the evidence presentation system. Move each exhibit in individually before publishing it, unless admitted by stipulation; raise known exhibit objections by the final pretrial conference. No examination beyond redirect and recross absent exceptional circumstances. To have the jury polled, ask at the pretrial conference and again promptly after the verdict.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Criminal sentencing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Criminal sentencing (trap): To get an evidentiary hearing on a PSR objection, expressly request it when filing the objection or the response (L.R. 83.9(c)). A party presenting witnesses at sentencing must file a Notice (Other) at least 14 days before the hearing, giving each witness’s legal name and estimated testimony time; late notice may mean exclusion.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Settlement and dismissal
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Settlement and dismissal: On a full settlement, promptly file a Notice of Settlement, then a Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(ii) stipulation signed by all parties who have appeared, including former parties (L.R. 68.1). When seeking dismissal, identify which provision of Rule 41 applies. In employment discrimination cases, a joint report on suitability for the Federal Mediation Program is due about 5.5 months before trial. Default and default judgment requests should use the court’s posted procedures and forms.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Dispositive motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Dispositive motions (trap): Except on subject matter jurisdiction, each party generally gets one dispositive motion per stage (one motion to dismiss, one summary judgment motion), one supporting memorandum per motion, and one response to each opposing motion. The limits apply per party, not per counsel; consolidated or joint responses are encouraged. Statements of undisputed material facts are not required and will not be considered unless jointly submitted. Factual assertions without proper record citation will not be considered. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery; motions to stay are granted only in unusual circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Page limits and replies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Page limits and replies (trap): Local Rule 7.1(b) limits exclude the cover sheet, tables of contents and authorities, and certificate of service. Noncompliant briefs may be disregarded or the motion summarily denied. Move to exceed sufficiently before the brief is due; such motions are rarely granted absent compelling reasons. Replies are not required (L.R. 7.1(c)); if one becomes necessary, it may not exceed 10 pages.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and hearings
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and hearings: The preferred communication is a formal motion filed on ECF. Anything conveyed by phone or email from chambers or clerk’s staff is not part of the record and does not bind the court. Copy all parties on any correspondence. Ex parte contact with staff is strongly discouraged; any contact must go to dumitru_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov, avoid the merits, and include all counsel of record. In-person conferences and hearings are strongly preferred; request telephonic participation well in advance by email. To request oral argument, file a separate motion with a memorandum of no more than 5 pages; the court gives weight to requests that give a young lawyer a chance to argue. Courtesy copies are not required unless requested; any paper copies must be bound, collated, and double-sided. Email proposed orders in Word to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling conference and ESI
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling conference and ESI: Be ready to discuss reasonable deadlines under Rule 16; counsel’s input gets significant weight. Before the conference, agree as far as possible on an ESI protocol covering sources and search limits, form of production, preservation, inadvertently produced privileged ESI, and cost allocation, and be ready to argue any disagreement. Extensions are entertained only if they do not affect the trial date or the court’s ability to decide dispositive motions, and must be sought by motion before the deadline, with the movant showing necessity. If the trial date changes, other dates stay in place.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): Discovery and all related motion practice must be completed by the deadline; serve requests early enough that responses and objections are resolved before it. The parties may continue by agreement afterward, but the court will not address disputes arising after the deadline. Bring disputes promptly, preferably by motion specifying the relief sought. If all parties agree a phone conference would avoid motion practice, request one by email to chambers. Per the form order, any Daubert motion must be filed before the discovery deadline, and the court should be told early if a Daubert hearing may be needed.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Form scheduling order deadlines
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Form scheduling order deadlines: Counted back from trial: plaintiff’s experts 21 weeks, defendant’s 17 weeks, rebuttal within 30 days after defendant’s; joinder and amendment 17 weeks; final witness list and notice on mediation 15 weeks; discovery 13 weeks; dispositive motions 11 weeks; pretrial disclosures (filed and served) 9 weeks; motions in limine 4 weeks; jury instructions 3 weeks; final pretrial conference no later than 2 weeks. Objections to designations and exhibits, and counter-designations, are due within 10 days after service. Also within 10 days of the pretrial disclosures, jointly submit (not file) electronic full deposition transcripts with each side’s designations highlighted in different colors, and electronic copies of all exhibits numbered continuously across parties with a master list. Disclose courtroom technology to the other side

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Motions in limine: Each party files a single motion listing all in limine issues with one brief of no more than 25 pages; the response is limited to 25 pages and any reply to 10. The court may reserve ruling until the issue arises at trial.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury instructions and findings
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Jury instructions and findings: File one set of joint proposed jury instructions, verdict forms, and interrogatories 3 weeks before trial, covering each claim, defense, element, burden, standard of proof, and type of relief, with authority; email Word copies to chambers. Phased trials need separate sets for each phase. For disputed items, each side submits its version with a brief, supported explanation; an item submitted in only one version is assumed agreed. Follow the form of the Sixth Circuit Pattern Jury Instructions, and certify that you conferred to resolve differences. Bench trials: proposed findings and conclusions with authority (L.R. 52.1) are due 4 weeks before trial, with facts in chronological order and conclusions stating elements, burden, standard, and remedy without argument; email them in WordPerfect or a compatible format.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Trial conduct (trap): Counsel appear at 9:00 a.m. for preliminary matters; trial starts at 9:30 a.m. Stand at the lectern to examine, never approach a witness without permission, and never stand near or lean on the jury box. Jurors may not question witnesses. Counsel may lead voir dire within limits, then submit challenges on the deputy’s form; no back-striking of previously seated jurors. Share any visuals, video, or audio for openings with opposing counsel before trial. Only one lawyer per side may examine and object during a given witness. Sidebars are discouraged; raise matters during breaks. Resolve the method for recorded testimony with the other side before trial. Know Local Rule 43.3 and give the deputy 3 copies of the exhibit list before trial. Stipulated exhibits need not be moved in individually. Exhibits that can be electronic must be, and j

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury deliberations and settlement
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Jury deliberations and settlement: Jurors may take notes during the proof but not openings or closings. During deliberations, give the deputy a mobile number and be able to return within 10 minutes. The deputy polls on request, and post-verdict juror contact will not be permitted absent extraordinary circumstances. Mediation or other ADR is urged in every case. Tell the court immediately upon settlement, and file a stipulation or agreed order of dismissal within 30 days or by the trial date, whichever is sooner.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling (trap): Scheduling orders are entered directly, without an in-person conference. Questions about the trial date go to the judicial assistant within 7 days of receiving the order; after that, a motion for continuance is required. Any schedule change requires a motion with a proposed agreed order; continuances need cause, and successive resettings need compelling necessity. If the trial date moves, all other dates stay unless the court orders otherwise. The form order counts back from trial: amendments, joinder, and all Rule 12 and Rule 56 motions due 150 days before (untimely dispositive motions may be summarily denied); employment discrimination cases file a joint mediation-suitability report at 150 days.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and courtesy copies: Written correspondence is discouraged; copy all counsel if you send it. Law clerks may be contacted (chambers 865-545-4762, ext. 2, or varlan_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov) but not about the merits; include all sides on calls and copy all counsel on emails. No courtesy hard copies unless the court asks; any requested copy must be printed after e-filing so it bears the ECF header. If you file on the day of a hearing or trial, notify chambers or the courtroom deputy by email or phone.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Hearings and page limits
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Hearings and page limits: Oral argument is decided case by case, and the court may set argument on its own. Out-of-town counsel wanting to appear by phone at a conference (other than the final pretrial conference, generally in person) must contact the judicial assistant at least 1 week ahead. Follow Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits; reasonable requests to exceed them may be granted in complex cases.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery and depositions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery and depositions (trap): Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting within 15 days of the scheduling order and file the discovery plan within 10 days after; the order lists specific e-discovery topics to resolve. Discovery, including evidence depositions, closes 90 days before trial, and motions to compel must be filed at least 30 days before that deadline. Discovery disputes follow three steps: meet and confer; a conference with the assigned magistrate judge (who may rule); and only then a written motion certifying compliance with both steps and Rule 37(a)(1). docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Experts and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Experts and Daubert (trap): Expert disclosures are due 150 days before trial for plaintiff and 120 days for defendant; rebuttal within 30 days after the other side’s disclosure. A motion for a Daubert hearing must be filed no later than 90 days before trial or challenges are waived. If a Daubert hearing is requested, file the challenged experts’ reports at least 5 days before the hearing.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Status report and pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Status report and pretrial order (trap): A joint status report is due on the discovery deadline, covering completion of discovery, whether argument would help on pending dispositive motions, planned pretrial motions, jury or nonjury and trial length, settlement and mediation, and other matters. Plaintiff serves a draft pretrial order 45 days before trial (47 if by mail); defendant responds within 5 working days. If no agreement after a face-to-face conference, plaintiff notifies chambers at least 31 days before trial. The agreed pretrial order is due 30 days before trial; failure may be treated as failure to prosecute.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial filings: Final witness lists 45 days before trial (supplement within 5 days after service). Rule 26(a)(3) disclosures, motions in limine, and jury instructions (or proposed findings and conclusions for bench trials) are due 30 days before trial. Motions in limine are generally heard at the final pretrial conference. Objections to deposition designations or exhibits meant to be treated as motions in limine need a supporting brief; undisclosed objections other than under Rules 402 and 403 are waived. Confer on exhibit authenticity and admissibility before the final pretrial conference. Trial briefs: the form order requires briefs on novel or unusual legal questions at least 15 days before trial, while the Judicial Preferences say at least 7 days; follow your case’s order. Give the courtroom deputy at least 5 working days’ notice before the pretr

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: Counsel arrive at 8:30 a.m. for preliminary matters; trial begins at 9 a.m. A case not reached is held in line for that week. Bring the original and one copy of labeled, numbered exhibits. The judge conducts preliminary voir dire and allows counsel to follow up; challenges go on a form, and back-striking is not permitted. One attorney per witness; examination beyond redirect and recross is generally not allowed. Keep sidebars to a minimum and give advance notice of videotaped testimony. Juror lists may be used only for jury selection and must be returned or destroyed afterward. Jurors may take notes except during openings and closings; exhibits go to the jury room except firearms and illegal narcotics.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Closing arguments (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Closing arguments (trap): Agree on time limits before closings and follow them strictly. Stay within arm’s length of the DEPS podium and no closer to the jury than its jury-side edge; remove flip-chart pages after use. Objections during closing must state only the legal ground. Refer to witnesses by proper names, not first names alone (unless commonly so called at trial), refer to opposing counsel only as “Plaintiff’s counsel” or “Defendants’ counsel,” and show no reaction to opposing argument.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Injunctions and settlement
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Injunctions and settlement: TROs and injunctions follow Rule 65; briefing as in other cases, and expedited discovery on motion. Do not send appellate filings. The judge encourages mediation and other ADR; magistrate judges may be involved case by case. To consent to trial by a magistrate judge, notify the judicial assistant.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Chambers copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Chambers copies (trap): For any dispositive motion, and any other motion or responsive pleading over 25 pages including attachments, mail or hand deliver a courtesy hard copy to chambers. Other courtesy copies are appreciated and go to the Clerk’s Office.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): File a separate, concise statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs, each supported by no more than two record citations. The opponent files, with its brief, a separate response to each fact stating that it is (1) undisputed, (2) undisputed only for the motion, or (3) disputed, with a specific record citation, and may add numbered additional disputed facts with citations. No argument in these statements; failure to file one may lead the court to strike the motion or opposition.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and conferences
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and conferences: Written correspondence is discouraged; if sent, copy all counsel. Law clerks may be contacted, but not on the merits. Telephone conferences are encouraged and are scheduled through Senior Law Clerk Penny Arning; save motions needing a court appearance for complicated matters the parties can’t agree on. Oral argument is decided case by case and may be requested. Requests to exceed Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits in complex cases are usually granted. Sealing requires strict compliance with Local Rule 26.2 and Procter & Gamble Co. v. Bankers Trust Co., 78 F.3d 219 (6th Cir. 1996).

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery and extensions (trap): Try to resolve disputes yourselves, then by telephone conference with the assigned magistrate judge; only then file a motion (which may be referred to the magistrate judge) with the Rule 37 certification. A standard case should finish discovery in 8 or 9 months and be ready for trial within 1 year. Except for the dispositive motion and Daubert deadlines and the trial date, deadlines may be modified by agreement of all counsel. Continuances are discouraged; lack of timely trial preparation is not good cause. In the sample orders, discovery closes 60 days before trial and motions to compel are due at least 30 days before that.

docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Experts and Daubert (trap): Sample orders: plaintiff’s experts 150 days before trial, defendant’s 120 days, rebuttal within 30 days after. A party offering a computer-generated animation must say so with its expert disclosures and give the animation to all parties 45 days before pretrial disclosures (or the close of expert discovery, if earlier).

docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial order (trap): File an agreed pretrial order 30 days before trial and email it to chambers in WordPerfect format. docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial

The court conducts preliminary voir dire and counsel may add questions; back-striking is not permitted.
