Only one lawyer per side may examine a witness, and examination beyond redirect and recross requires compelling circumstances. Stipulate to as many exhibits as possible; stipulated exhibits need not be moved individually. Time limits for openings and closings are agreed at trial and enforced. Give the courtroom deputy advance notice of vide

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Jury: A charge conference is held after the close of proof, where additional instruction requests are considered. Counsel may propose verdict forms, but the court prepares the form submitted. Jurors may take notes and take properly admitted exhibits into deliberations. During deliberations, be able to return within 10 minutes. The court polls every jury, and counsel may not interview jurors after verdict absent extraordinary circumstances (L.R. 48.1).

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Bench trials
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Bench trials: Proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law, which serve as final argument, are filed after trial (the sample sets 30 days), supported by authority, and emailed to chambers in WordPerfect format. Facts go in chronological order as proved at trial; conclusions must be concise and not argumentative.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Injunctions, ADR, and criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Injunctions, ADR, and criminal cases: Rule 65 is strictly applied, and extraordinary relief is granted only in extraordinary circumstances. Expedited discovery requires compelling circumstances and may not be used in cases that clearly do not qualify for Rule 65 relief. Mediation, arbitration, and other ADR are encouraged, and reasonable extensions to pursue them are usually granted. In criminal cases, the assigned magistrate judge controls pretrial preparation; trial practice is the same as in civil cases.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): Statements of undisputed facts are not required and will not be considered unless jointly submitted; follow Rule 56’s record-citation standards instead. Before any summary judgment motion, the parties must confer and build a single joint appendix of exhibits, consecutively paginated with a table of contents, filed by the movant with the first motion and cited by page number. Include only cited deposition pages. The non-movant may add a consecutively numbered addendum with its opposition. Material outside the appendix and addendum will not be considered. Each party gets only one motion to dismiss and one summary judgment motion (jurisdictional issues excepted), one supporting memorandum per motion, and one response per opposing motion; consolidated or joint responses are encouraged.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Briefing limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Briefing limits (trap): Replies are not required (L.R. 7.1(c)); any reply is capped at 10 pages, and only the first 10 pages of a longer reply will be considered. Requests for 5 extra pages in opening and answering briefs are typically granted in sufficiently complex cases but rarely for replies; move at least 10 days before the brief is due, if the schedule allows. Extension motions must be filed well before the deadline and specifically define the reasons for and length of the extension. Contacting a law clerk does not extend any deadline; only a timely motion can.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Hearings and communications
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Hearings and communications: Oral argument is set when the court finds it useful. To request it, file a separate motion with a memorandum of no more than 5 pages; the court weighs whether argument offers a speaking opportunity for a young lawyer. At scheduled hearings, be ready to present evidence; failing to arrange it is no ground for a continuance. Emergency (Rule 65) hearings are often set the same day the petition is filed; pre-hearing briefing is welcome. Correspondence may not substitute for motions and must be copied to all parties. To speak with a law clerk, email mcdonough_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov explaining why, with a callback number. No printed courtesy copies unless requested.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Case management conference: The court usually holds an in-person case-management conference at the start of each case. Every lawyer who will actively handle discovery, motions, or trial must attend in person, ready to discuss legal theories, disputed facts, anticipated evidence, and the Rule 16(a) and 16(c)(2) topics. Out-of-district lawyers are encouraged to use local counsel. Typical deadlines before trial: expert disclosures, joinder, and amendments 29 weeks; rebuttal experts 25 weeks; final witness list 23 weeks; discovery close 19 weeks; dispositive and Daubert motions 15 weeks; pretrial disclosures 6 weeks; motions in limine 5 weeks; jury instructions or proposed findings 3 weeks; final pretrial conference the Monday two weeks before trial. Discovery typically takes about 8 months. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery, and stays a

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery: Confer before raising disputes; leave from a magistrate judge is not needed to file a discovery motion. Do not contact the opposing side’s experts. Rebuttal experts may only challenge the opinions or methods of a previously disclosed expert, no broader in scope. Discovery, including evidence depositions, expert depositions, and requests for admission, must be completed by the cut-off. Confidentiality agreements bind the parties, but sealing requires Local Rule 26.2 and the sealing order entered at the start of the case.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions in limine and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Motions in limine and Daubert (trap): Each party may file only one motion in limine identifying all evidence to be excluded, with one brief of no more than 25 pages; separately filed motions in limine will be summarily denied. Attach the challenged evidence where practicable. Motions to exclude expert testimony under Rule 702 must be filed by the Daubert deadline; they will not be entertained as motions in limine.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Final pretrial conference (trap): The final pretrial conference (3 p.m., Courtroom 3, Chattanooga) must be attended in person. Submit an agreed final pretrial order following the posted sample by the conference; it supplants the pleadings, so include your jury demand to avoid a waiver argument. File trial briefs on anticipated evidentiary and legal issues at least 3 business days before the conference. Before the conference, file an exhibit list and provide pre-marked exhibits, and be ready to argue admissibility; unprepared counsel risk adverse rulings. Jury instructions are submitted as one joint proposal, with competing versions of unresolved instructions, all with citations (L.R. 7.4), and emailed to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Trial (trap): Counsel lead voir dire under the court’s direction: for-cause challenges first, then peremptories; jurors called later are seated at the end of the box, and no back-striking. Openings and closings rarely exceed 30 minutes per party. Share any visual, video, or audio aids with opposing counsel before use. Examine from the lectern, standing if able; one attorney per witness for questioning and objections. Offer each exhibit when it is authenticated and its admissibility established, not at the end of testimony or of your case. Give the courtroom deputy three copies of the exhibit list before trial. No vouching, testifying, or ad hominem attacks in closing. All exhibits that can be electronic must be; jurors view them electronically, and firearms and controlled substances stay out of the jury room. During deliberations, be able to re

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Criminal cases: Plea and motion deadlines set by the magistrate judge are enforced unless modified by motion to the court. Be ready to justify appeal or § 2255 waivers in Rule 11(c)(1)(A) or (B) agreements. Brady material is deemed requested at the defendant’s first appearance with counsel, and the government should disclose exculpatory and mitigating information as soon as practicable; early Jencks production is encouraged. Rule 17(c)(1) pretrial subpoenas require a motion, filed well before the plea deadline and trial.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Settlement and referrals
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Settlement and referrals: Tell the court immediately upon settlement and promptly file a stipulation or agreed order of dismissal, in any event before the trial date (L.R. 68.1). Social Security and ERISA dispositive motions are typically referred to a magistrate judge for a recommendation.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Contacting chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Contacting chambers (trap): Before calling chambers with a case question, review the docket and the Local Rules, and have the docket available during the call. Only requests for settlement conferences and status conferences may be made by faxed letter; a status-conference request must briefly state the reason. Everything else requires a written motion, and chambers staff cannot grant relief by phone.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Confidential position papers and status updates
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Confidential position papers and status updates: Send confidential position papers, and status updates only when directed by the court or staff, to EWD_Com@lamd.uscourts.gov as PDF attachments formatted under the Local Rules. Nothing else may be emailed there, and ex parte email communication is not permitted.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Proposed orders and judgments
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Proposed orders and judgments: Proposed orders go with the e-filed motion (last page or attachment) and must also be emailed in an editable format such as Word to ewd_orders@lamd.uscourts.gov with the case number in the subject line. Proposed judgments, when ordered, are emailed in Word and not filed in CM/ECF; subject line “Proposed Judgment - [case number] EWD.”

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Diversity jurisdiction: citizenship (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Diversity jurisdiction: citizenship (trap): The Notice applies to complaints and notices of removal (and the citizenship parts to Rule 7.1(a)(2) statements) in cases assigned to the judge that invoke 28 U.S.C. § 1332; the court screens all new filings. Allege an individual’s domicile and citizenship, not residence; both state of incorporation and principal place of business for a corporation; and every member of an LLC or partnership by name, through all layers. Negative allegations (“not a citizen of Louisiana”) are insufficient, and intervenors’ or joined parties’ citizenship must be alleged when leave is sought. If a non-named party removes claiming to be the correct defendant, allege citizenship of both it and the named defendant. Failure to establish citizenship of all parties requires remand.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Diversity jurisdiction: amount in controversy on removal (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Diversity jurisdiction: amount in controversy on removal (trap): Usually sufficient: a petition with an art. 893 statement or an affirmative over-$75,000 allegation (or wrongful-death/survival claims); a good-faith pre-removal demand over $75,000 (for a “policy limits” demand, proof the plaintiff knew the limits); an unequivocal discovery admission; or records showing damages over $75,000. Without such evidence, these are insufficient in personal-injury removals: conclusory statements, boilerplate damage categories, general injury descriptions, disc or spinal diagnoses and treatment without documented medical expenses over $25,000, no art. 893 statement, refusal to sign a damages stipulation, or citing other cases’ awards. In insurance-contract cases, policy limits or unquantified damage allegations generally don’t suffice; use an over-$75,000 demand o

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Pretrial order
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Pretrial order: Plaintiff’s counsel prepares the Pretrial Order with all parties’ cooperation, signed by all counsel; a party disagreeing with any part attaches an Opposition before submission. It covers jurisdiction, pending motions, each party’s claims, established facts, exhibits, witnesses, proposed amendments, settlement or ADR possibilities, jury or non-jury status, and each side’s time estimate. For each exhibit state only whether authenticity is objected to and why; admissibility objections go by motion in limine and pretrial memoranda on a schedule set at the pretrial conference. Absent good cause, only listed exhibits and witnesses are allowed.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Witnesses and depositions at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Witnesses and depositions at trial (trap): Will-call witnesses must be produced or subpoenaed and kept available, and a party may not release one without the other side’s express written or on-the-record consent. Designate deposition portions for the court and all parties no later than 21 days before trial. Video depositions are capped at 30 minutes and read depositions at 30 pages; file a written transcript of any video deposition into evidence, and supply a reader for any transcript read. Edit objections out of the tape or transcript; deposition objections needing a ruling are due to the court 14 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Jury instructions and courtroom (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Jury instructions and courtroom (trap): Joint jury instructions, including a joint verdict or interrogatory form, are filed by the scheduling-order deadline. No separate filings are allowed: disagreements go in footnotes with case authority and pinpoint citations. Fifth Circuit pattern instructions may be cited by number and edition. Courtroom 5 is fully electronic; present exhibits by laptop or document camera, and arrange training before trial with courtroom deputy Brandy Lemelle Route (the notice lists (225) 389-3584; the page lists (225) 389-3588 for the deputy).

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Exhibits attached to filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Exhibits attached to filings (trap): Any pleading, motion, memorandum, opposition, or brief that attaches exhibits must include, as a separate CM/ECF attachment, an Exhibit List giving the caption, a descriptive title, the exhibit numbers or letters, and a description of each exhibit. File each exhibit separately; no in globo exhibits (attachments to affidavits and depositions may stay with them but must be shown on the list). Each exhibit’s docket description must match the Exhibit List. This division rule controls over any conflicting Administrative Procedures.

docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Media must not contact the courtroom deputy, docket clerk, or chambers.

docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Pretrial order (trap): Plaintiff’s counsel prepares the Pretrial Order with all parties’ cooperation, signed by all counsel, after conferring on stipulated facts, eliminating uncontested claims, and exchanging trial exhibits. docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Jury instructions and verdict forms (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Jury instructions and verdict forms (trap): 28 days before every civil jury trial, submit one joint proposed draft of the final charge after a good-faith effort to agree. Disputed instructions are numbered and embedded where desired, each with a footnote stating the objection and the proponent’s response; the court aims to circulate a draft charge ruling on the objections before trial. Confer on a verdict form; if no agreement, separate forms may be filed, highlighting the agreed interrogatories, and pocket briefs of no more than 5 pages on the other side’s form are due within 7 days. Objections may be preserved at the charge conference. The older Uniform Pretrial Notice allows separate filings on disputed items and lets Fifth Circuit pattern instructions be cited by number and edition.

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Impeachment evidence (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Impeachment evidence (trap): To use documents or evidence solely for impeachment that are not on the Pretrial Order or not exchanged in discovery, file a motion for leave to file a sealed motion for in-camera inspection no later than 30 days before trial, attaching the evidence and briefly explaining what it impeaches and how. (The Uniform Pretrial Notice says simply to submit it under seal for in camera inspection by the same deadline.)

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Depositions at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Depositions at trial (trap): Designate the portions of written or video depositions to be read or shown no later than 28 days before trial, after conferring and redacting irrelevant and redundant material, including colloquies between counsel. Only necessary portions may be used. Motions in limine on deposition objections are due 21 days before trial and must identify each objected-to question by page and line with a concise objection. Give the courtroom deputy redacted transcripts at trial, and supply a reader for any transcript to be read.

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Voir dire and bench trials
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Voir dire and bench trials: Each party submits proposed voir dire questions; to question the panel directly, state the reasons and estimate the time needed. The judge’s posted standard voir dire covers eligibility, juror cards, panel questions, case-specific questions, and party questions only “as approved by Court”; the court reads a brief case description circulated to the parties before trial. In non-jury trials only, submit proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law.

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Exhibits and courtroom technology
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Exhibits and courtroom technology: Each party submits an Electronic Bench Book through CM/ECF (Utilities / Evidence Upload) before trial or evidentiary proceedings, at the time set in the order; it is for the court only. Name files by exhibit number, part, and description (e.g., “1-a_photograph.jpg”), mark sealed exhibits “SEALED,” note redactions, and keep files under 500MB (split video into 10-minute clips). JERS is not used by counsel to present evidence: use a laptop connection or the document camera in Courtroom 1, and keep trial exhibits matching the uploaded numbers and images. Arrange equipment training with courtroom deputy Kristie Causey (225-389-3574) before trial. Admitted exhibits stay with the offering party until appeal time runs (L.R. 79).

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Settlement affidavit
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Settlement affidavit: By the scheduling-order deadline, counsel for each party files an affidavit stating the date and time of a settlement conference of counsel. Plaintiff’s counsel attests to a good-faith offer and conveying the counteroffer; defense counsel attests to conveying the offer and making a good-faith counteroffer. State no dollar amounts. The Pretrial Order must also state the settlement history and whether the parties want a settlement conference before a magistrate judge, plus jury or non-jury status and each side’s time estimate.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling and contact
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Scheduling and contact: No standard days or times for any matter, except Nashville jury trials, which start Tuesdays at 9:00 a.m. Courtroom 6C; courtroom deputy (615) 736-7157. Correspondence with the court is discouraged; when permitted, serve it on opposing counsel, and it will be filed as public record (confidential settlement statements excepted). No telephone calls with the law clerks. Requests to take part in case management or other conferences by telephone must be made in advance by written motion.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Chambers copies
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Chambers copies: Judge Trauger does not want chamber copies of filings unless the judge requests them.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Case management
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Case management: Judge Trauger holds the initial case management conference personally. File a joint proposed initial case management order 3 business days before it, and lead counsel for all parties must attend. With rare exceptions, a firm trial date is set at the initial conference and will not be moved. Pro se cases go to a magistrate judge for case management. The sample order calls for a Joint Mediation Report saying whether the parties will mediate and, if so, the mediator and date.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Extensions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Extensions and continuances (trap): Agreed extensions are routinely granted, except for dispositive motion deadlines; trial continuances are rarely granted. Make requests in writing and state opposing counsel’s position if possible.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Motions and briefing (trap): Briefs may not exceed 25 pages. Replies are optional on dispositive motions; on other motions, replies need leave. Under the sample order, responses to dispositive motions are due 21 days after filing and optional replies 10 days after the response. No partial summary judgment motion without leave: first file a separate motion justifying it in terms of overall economy of time and expense. Oral argument is granted when appropriate or beneficial. Dispositive motions are not referred to the magistrate judge, except in pro se cases.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): 40 interrogatories, including subparts (the sample order expands Local Rule 33.01(b)). No discovery motion may be filed until the parties have conferred in good faith and then scheduled and taken part in a conference call with Judge Trauger. Where a magistrate judge is managing the case, that judge resolves discovery disputes, and most discovery motions are referred. Discovery is not stayed during dispositive motions unless ordered. Protective orders and confidentiality agreements are considered case by case.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Expert testimony in writing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Expert testimony in writing (trap): In civil cases and some criminal cases, expert testimony (other than medical) must be reduced to writing before trial and is read at trial as the expert’s direct testimony. Departures are considered case by case. Challenge an expert’s qualifications by motion in limine.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — TROs
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. TROs: TRO papers must state efforts made to contact the other side. The judge deciding the TRO may not be the assigned judge; for a TRO sought after the case starts, advise the presiding judge’s secretary. Expedited discovery requires a written motion showing good cause.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Pretrial: An agreed proposed pretrial order is due no later than the pretrial conference; contents and timing are set in the order setting the case for trial. Pretrial briefs are not routinely required in jury cases. Motions in limine must be filed and answered before the pretrial conference, per the trial order’s deadlines; the judge tries to rule on them at the conference. Requests to accommodate out-of-town parties, witnesses, or lawyers go by written motion at the earliest opportunity or at a pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Trial: Trial days run 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with a one-hour lunch; no trailer dockets for civil trials. After the court’s voir dire, counsel question the whole panel; peremptory strikes are made simultaneously on written forms (duplicate strikes possible), and cause challenges at the bench. Juror copies are allowed with advance notice. File agreed jury instructions in hard copy and on disk, one per page with a heading, and disputed ones with citations, by the deadline set at the pretrial conference. No interim commentary by counsel; only one lawyer may examine a given witness. Raise matters outside the jury’s presence at recesses. The judge polls the ju

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Criminal cases: A pretrial conference is set once it is clear the case will be tried. Do not assume a trial continuance will be granted. Notify the courtroom deputy by phone or email as soon as a plea is decided and suggest timing; deliver the drafted plea petition, any plea agreement, and the government’s statement of elements and penalties to chambers before the plea.

docs.t: Judge Chip Frensley (M.D. Tenn.) — Chambers and contact
docs.x: Judge Chip Frensley, M.D. Tenn.. Chambers and contact: Email proposed case management orders to frensleychambers@tnmd.uscourts.gov. No chambers copies of filings unless the judge requests them. Correspondence, other than for scheduling, is discouraged; any permitted letter must be served on opposing counsel and is filed as public record unless directed otherwise. Contact law clerks only for scheduling questions and never about the merits. Requests for out-of-town counsel to appear by phone must be made by motion well in advance. Telephone conferences are not recorded (the judge usually enters an order reciting the outcome); a record requires an in-court proceeding.

docs.t: Judge Chip Frensley (M.D. Tenn.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Chip Frensley, M.D. Tenn.. Discovery disputes (trap): Counsel must actually talk about the disputed issues before raising them, and the LR 37.01(b)(3) certification must say they have spoken. A motion to compel, for protective order, or for sanctions will be denied if counsel have not spoken, or if it is uncertain whether they have. Raise unresolved disputes promptly by requesting a telephonic discovery conference or by motion; either way the parties must file a joint discovery dispute statement describing the specific requests and each side’s position with facts and authority. Motions to compel or for protective order must address Rule 26(b)(1) proportionality. No speaking objections at depositions; state objections concisely (“hearsay,” “a conclusion”) without argument. Raise needs for more or fewer than 25 interrogatories at a case management conference or by motion.

docs.t: Judge Chip Frensley (M.D. Tenn.) — Case management orders
docs.x: Judge Chip Frensley, M.D. Tenn.. Case management orders: The judge generally uses the referring district judge’s standard order, or the judge’s own form if none. Include any special discovery or case management procedures in the proposed order. If the parties disagree, do not submit separate proposed orders; state each side’s proposal under each section of one order. Email a Word copy to the courtroom deputy the same day the proposed order is filed, and read the Notice of Setting of Initial Case Management Conference. No initial case management conferences are usually set in pro se cases, but scheduling orders are entered; pro se litigants must follow the Local Rules and these guidelines.

docs.t: Judge Chip Frensley (M.D. Tenn.) — Extensions and modifications (trap)
docs.x: Judge Chip Frensley, M.D. Tenn.. Extensions and modifications (trap): Motions to modify a case management order or deadline must be filed at least seven days before the earliest affected deadline. Unless joint, they must confirm the movant conferred with opposing counsel and state any objection. The motion must list all deadlines, even unaffected ones, state that dispositive motion deadlines (including responses and replies) will still be at least 90 days before trial (LR 16.01(d)(2.f)), and detail the movant’s diligence and good cause under Rule 16(b)(4). The judge will not modify schedules in ways that affect a district-judge trial date. If a trial continuance is needed, style it as a motion to continue trial asking that the schedule changes be referred to the magistrate judge. docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Case resolution: About 14 days after fact discovery closes, file a joint report confirming a good-faith attempt to resolve the case and stating whether ADR might help. A request for a judicial settlement conference must explain why mediation is not feasible, propose timing, and state any preferred magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Pretrial: Submit a joint proposed pretrial order before the pretrial conference containing: a statement that it supplants the pleadings, jurisdiction, each side’s theory (1 page maximum each), the issues (marking jury and court issues), relief sought, anticipated evidentiary disputes, and estimated trial length. Motions in limine must comply with L.R. 7.01(a)(1) and be filed and answered before the pretrial conference, where the judge tries to rule on them. Give notice of an anticipated JMOL motion no later than the pretrial conference, with a brief.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Trial: Trial days run 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with a one-hour lunch. After counsel’s voir dire, cause challenges are made at the bench, then peremptory strikes simultaneously on written forms. Exhibits must be premarked numerically and placed in binders, each party’s set in a different color. Show exhibits to opposing counsel first and have an extra copy for the court; exhibit and witness lists go to the court, deputy, reporter, and opposing counsel on day one. Juror copies of admitted exhibits need advance notice. File agreed jury instructions and email a copy to the courtroom deputy, one per page with a heading; file disputed instructions with citations by the same deadline. No interim commentary; only one lawyer may examine a given witness. Raise matters outside the jury’s presence at recesses. The judge polls the jury in every case.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Criminal cases: A status conference is set about 45 days before trial and a pretrial conference about 1 week before. A motion to continue trial must be filed with a Waiver of Speedy Trial Rights signed by the defendant. Notify the courtroom deputy by phone or email as soon as a plea is decided and suggest timing; deliver the drafted plea petition, any plea agreement, and the government’s statement of elements and penalties to chambers before the plea.

docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Defendants must answer even if they have filed or plan to file a motion to dismiss or for judgment; the motion does not delay the answer deadline. Lead counsel must confer in person to prepare written stipulations of uncontested facts for dispositive motions, filed by the court-set date (or a joint notice that there are none). These are mandatory.

docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Briefing format and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Requests for a conference on non-discovery issues require a letter certifying good-faith efforts and outlining the issues. Non-motion correspondence is not docketed but is kept in the public case f

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Contact with chambers
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Contact with chambers: No ex parte communications. Counsel may contact the courtroom deputy, judicial assistant, or law clerks on procedural matters only. Continuances are rarely granted; in civil cases a continuance motion must be signed by the parties themselves.

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial preparation
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial preparation: Lead counsel and parties attend the final pretrial with full authority; counsel must confer with clients and each other on final settlement posture at least 2 business days before. Each side gets a set number of hours for its whole case. Exchange proposed jury instructions 10 calendar days before the final pretrial, then file one joint submission (agreed, plaintiff’s opposed, defendant’s opposed) with citations; objections must give reasons and authority, not just “objection.” Submit only case-specific law; the court gives boilerplate instructions. Bring a CD with the instructions, the joint preliminary statement (1 page), proposed voir dire, and witness list to the final pretrial. Trial briefs, witness and exhibit lists, and motions in limine are due by the court-set date, with exhibits exchanged at least 1 week earlier; unlisted wi

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Trial: Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. with a 1-hour lunch and two 15-minute breaks (the practices page says 5:00 p.m.); counsel must be in the courtroom from 8:30 a.m. Parties must be present whenever the jury is seated. The court conducts voir dire, then one counsel per party briefly questions the panel (about 10 minutes per party). Peremptories use an “informed strike” method by rounds; a pass forfeits that challenge, and consecutive passes by both sides end challenges. Examinations need not be from the lectern; ask permission to approach a witness. Show any opening-statement exhibits to opposing counsel in advance. Jurors may take notes and submit written questions. Raise Daubert challenges well before trial, and arrange daily transcripts.

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases (trap): A plea under a written plea agreement must be taken by the pretrial conference date; the practices page also describes a change-of-plea deadline about 2 weeks before trial after which no plea agreements are accepted. The defendant must attend the pretrial and final pretrial. Written pleas are strongly preferred; binding agreements are acceptable. Motions other than motions in limine are due within 30 days after arraignment. By 3 business days before the final pretrial: stipulations signed by counsel and the defendant, a joint preliminary statement (up to 2 pages), trial briefs, exhibit lists, motions in limine, proposed voir dire, and the joint jury instructions; witness lists are emailed to chambers only (not filed or exchanged). Exhibit objections by noon 1 business day before the final pretrial. Jencks and reciprocal Jencks material

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: The CMC is held by telephone: counsel for all parties get on one line and call the court at 216-357-7160. Lead counsel must participate; a motion to excuse lead counsel for undue hardship is due at least 7 days before the CMC. The Rule 26(f) meeting is arranged by plaintiff’s counsel (defense counsel in removed cases), with initial disclosures at or within 10 days after it. File the Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting on the court’s form at least 3 working days before the CMC, including an e-discovery plan or agreement to the Appendix K default standard. Plaintiff’s counsel must confirm that the defendant’s counsel (or an unrepresented defendant) received the CMC order. If the case resolves before the CMC, submit a jointly signed stipulation of settlement or dismissal or notify the court that one is coming.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Early settlement demand (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Early settlement demand (trap): Plaintiffs must give defendants a written demand with a description and monetary breakdown of damages at least 1 week before the CMC, and defendants must respond with an offer no later than the CMC date.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment and courtesy copies (trap): No summary judgment motion before discovery closes without express leave, and all summary judgment arguments go in a single motion; multiple summary judgment motions need express leave. Submit courtesy copies to chambers of all dispositive motions, oppositions, and replies, with all supporting material.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Contacting chambers: No ex parte calls to chambers on substantive issues, including case management deadlines, requests to file briefing, or the status of pending motions; file a motion on the public docket instead. Routine calls (such as dial-in information) are acceptable, and a deposition dispute needing immediate help may be raised by a joint call.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Continuances (trap): A trial or hearing continuance in a civil case requires a written motion stating the reason, endorsed in writing by all parties and lead counsel of record. A motion based on a conflicting trial assignment must attach a copy of that assignment and be filed within 15 days after counsel learns of the conflict and at least 30 days before trial (the criminal order has the same timing but no endorsement requirement).

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial filings (trap): Trials are set at 8:30 a.m. in Courtroom 15A. A final pretrial conference is set on any party’s request; parties and lead counsel must attend, and lead counsel files a status report 5 days before it. Trial briefs (facts, law, witness list with subjects, exhibit index, evidentiary issues, and, for jury trials, proposed voir dire and jury instructions) are due 5 days before a jury trial or 10 days before a bench trial, and exchanged 5 days before trial. Unlisted witnesses (lay or expert) testify only in extraordinary circumstances; unlisted exhibits need good cause. Stipulations of uncontested facts are due 10 days before trial, prepared after an in-person conference; no examination is allowed on facts that could have been stipulated. A joint statement of disputed facts is due 5 days before a jury trial or 10 days before a benc

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Exhibits, depositions, and instructions
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Exhibits, depositions, and instructions: Deliver one copy of each exhibit to chambers (not the Clerk) at least 2 days before trial and exchange exhibits and indexes by then. Plaintiffs use numbers and defendants letters (double letters after 26), with party name prefixes in multiparty cases, “Jt. Ex.” for joint exhibits, and every page of a multipage exhibit separately numbered (1-1, 1-2). Binders with tabs and a table of contents are recommended. Give 5 days’ notice before trial of deposition testimony to be used; written objections are due 4 days before trial and the proponent’s reply 2 days after. Video depositions need a complete written transcript. Counsel must confer in person on jury instructions, identify agreed and disputed instructions (with separate authority for each), and email agreed instructions to BetsyAnn_Breese@ohnd.uscourts.gov (or on

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Remote testimony and courtroom technology
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Remote testimony and courtroom technology: Remote witness testimony requires prior court approval and contact with the court’s technology staff at least 10 days before trial. It is not for witnesses who would merely be inconvenienced or to save cost, only for witnesses otherwise unavailable, on sufficient cause. To see the courtroom equipment, contact the courtroom deputy (216-357-7160) at least 1 week before trial. During jury deliberations counsel must stay near the courtroom and notify the deputy before leaving the area.

docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases (trap): Trial is set about 6 weeks after arraignment, with a pretrial about 2 weeks after arraignment and a final pretrial 1 week before trial. No plea agreement is accepted later than 1 week before trial. Discovery is due 1 week after the first pretrial, and the court will not continue trial for a discovery failure; notify the court in writing immediately. Pretrial motions are due 1 week before the final pretrial, responses by the final pretrial; pro forma motions are disfavored. By 4:00 p.m. two days before trial, submit a jointly prepared neutral statement of the case, written stipulations signed by counsel and defendant, voir dire questions and jury instructions (the court follows Sixth Circuit and Federal Judicial Center patterns), evidentiary memoranda, and any written hypothetical questions with authority. Exchange demonstratives 2

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Briefs: length and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Briefs: length and format (trap): Local Rule 7.1(f) page limits are strictly enforced; parties may instead use word limits: Expedited 3,500; Administrative, Standard, and Unassigned 7,000; Complex 11,000; Mass Tort 15,000 (still include the L.R. 7.1(f) certification). Briefs over 7,500 words need a table of contents and table of authorities. Pictures, simple tables, and graphs don’t count and are preferred in the text. One-inch margins, double-spaced, at least 12-point Times New Roman, Century Schoolbook, or similar; footnotes at least 10-point in the same typeface; citations in the text, not footnotes. Memoranda with excessive or long footnotes, or formatting liberties, will be struck. File text-searchable PDFs, preferably with bookmarks and hyperlinks. Motions to exceed length must be filed well in advance; one filed with the overlong brief will be

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Motion practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Motion practice (trap): Parties on the same side must file one joint brief (noting any argument a party does not join), and the opponent files one response. For cross-motions the court prefers a four-brief schedule (opening; combined cross-motion and response; combined response and reply; reply). No surreplies without leave, rarely given. Replies should not raise new evidence or arguments. Notices of supplemental authority may not exceed 350 words and must cite a PageID or point argued orally. Motions for reconsideration, however styled, are limited to 2 pages (or 500 words) or will be struck; no response unless the court asks. Don’t file proposed orders unless requested, and send no courtesy copies unless ordered (a requested copy must show the CM/ECF header). TRO, PI, and emergency motions must certify that the motion is necessary after conferring

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Record citations and exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Record citations and exhibits (trap): Depositions, deposition exhibits, and exhibits to a dispositive motion must be filed separately before the motion that cites them, and cited by ECF No. and PageID # in all dispositive and pretrial motions. Never refile a document already on the record; cite the earlier version. Save cited internet materials as PDFs on the record. Use full-page transcripts (not minuscripts), give exhibits meaningful docket names, and strip old ECF headers from previously filed documents.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Pleadings, jurisdiction, and dismissals (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Pleadings, jurisdiction, and dismissals (trap): An answer is required even if a Rule 12 motion is filed or planned; the motion does not extend the answer deadline, and a Rule 12(b)(6) motion may be treated as one under Rule 12(c). Beyond L.R. 3.13, corporate disclosures must state the state of incorporation and principal place of business; LLCs, partnerships, and similar entities must give that for the entity and each member. Omissions will lead to dismissal or remand for failure to establish jurisdiction. Amendments (by motion or as of right) must attach a redline or comparison, and a motion must say whether the defendant consents under Rule 15(a)(2). Dismiss fewer than all parties or claims by Rule 21 motion (stating whether anyone objects), not Rule 41; Rule 41 filings for that purpose will be struck.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Rule 26(f) report and case management conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Rule 26(f) report and case management conference (trap): Exchange initial disclosures preferably at least 7 days before the Rule 26(f) conference (otherwise within 14 days after it, and be ready to explain why). Schedule the conference no later than receipt of the CMC notice, and include any pro se party. Use the judge’s Rule 26(f) Report form. Each party must physically (not electronically) sign it; entity signers must state their title and have authority to bind. The form also requires a litigation-funding disclosure of anyone with a financial interest, funding role, interest in proceeds, or control over strategy or settlement, which may be emailed ex parte to chambers and must be updated. The CMC is in person unless all parties move to go virtual at least 7 calendar days ahead, after filing the report. Motions to reschedule or to excuse or require

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion of any kind (compel, quash, protective order, subpoena, sanctions) may be filed until counsel confer in person or by phone (not just email or text), then contact chambers at (216) 357-7265 or Calabrese_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov for a phone or Zoom conference. The court may then call for letters of up to 2 pages before setting any briefing. Boilerplate and general objections are generally treated as waiving all objections, including privilege. Burden objections must explain or quantify the burden. A party unsure about responsiveness may submit documents for in camera review. Serve requests early enough that responses are due before the cut-off (e.g., 31 days ahead for a 30-day response). Disclose lay trial witnesses at least 30 days before the discovery cut-off or they will be precluded. Rebuttal expert

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Depositions (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Depositions (trap): Local Rule 30.1 is strictly enforced. Objections are limited to “Objection, Form” or “Objection, Foundation” unless the questioner asks for the reason or privilege is asserted. Interjections such as “if you know” or “if you remember” are treated as coaching. Don’t interrupt answers, repeat or paraphrase prior testimony (defending counsel’s repetition counts as a speaking objection), or mislead the witness. Evasive answers are treated as a failure to testify and may bring an additional deposition; yes-or-no questions get yes, no, or a statement that they can’t be answered that way. Agreements to change the 7-hour limit are enforced only if in writing; 7 hours means on the record, excluding breaks.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Sealing and redaction
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Sealing and redaction: Redactions (generally a few words) require a motion for leave, typically at least 7 days before the deadline, explaining each redaction, certifying conferral with the producing party and its position, and emailing chambers an unredacted copy with proposed redactions marked. Sealing an entire document is allowed only rarely. A confidentiality designation under a protective order is not enough; the movant must justify sealing document by document under Shane Group. Once approved, file the redacted version, serve the unredacted version, and file it under seal.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment, conferences, and settlement
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment, conferences, and settlement: One summary judgment motion per party without leave; no responsive summary judgment motion unless ordered (all dispositive motions are due on the CMO deadline), and motions in limine may not substitute for summary judgment. Tell the court when the deadline is set if cross-motions are expected. For a status conference, give the court and other parties a summary of each issue at least 3 days ahead. Scheduling conflicts with court-set conferences: confer and file a notice with the reason and 3 alternative dates (not for trial dates or CMO deadlines). Contact chambers by phone or email only for discovery issues and scheduling. Final pretrial: lead trial counsel, parties (for entities, the person most familiar with the facts, not in-house counsel), and a representative with full and final authority up to the

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Newer lawyers
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Newer lawyers: If a notice is filed before the ruling saying a lawyer with 5 or fewer years in practice will argue all or a material part of a motion (including objections to an R&R), the court will hear oral argument. Requests to split witness examinations or arguments at trial should be raised at the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases (trap): Lead counsel must attend all proceedings, and the defendant must attend the final pretrial and trial. Trial-date changes need a written motion at least 2 days before the final pretrial citing 18 U.S.C. § 3161(h)(7)(B) factors; conflict-based continuances must identify the other case and judge and be filed within 15 days of learning of it and at least 30 days before trial. Responses to any motion are due in 7 days unless set otherwise; travel motions filed within 48 hours of travel are denied absent emergency. The government must answer discovery requests within 1 week; motions to compel are due within 1 week of a denial or non-response, and requests are docketed as notices. The order includes a sua sponte Brady directive, with in camera review of favorable but arguably immaterial information. Plea agreements go to chambers by e

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Motions to dismiss and early conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Motions to dismiss and early conference (trap): Chambers schedules an Initial Telephone Conference once the defendant appears; be ready to brief the judge on the facts, settlement talks, and key issues. The CMC is set during that call. No motion to dismiss may be filed before the Initial Telephone Conference. The judge requires counsel to discuss the basis for any such motion and routinely lets plaintiff amend to cure; an answer date falling before the conference is automatically tolled.

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment pre-motion letters (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment pre-motion letters (trap): No summary judgment motion may be filed until counsel meet and confer and exchange letters. The movant briefly outlines the merits with key record and legal citations; the opponent responds in writing identifying the genuine disputes of material fact. Keep letters short (bullet points encouraged); sample letters are posted on the judge’s page. File the letters as a joint attachment to a Motion for a Telephone Conference. The judge then discusses the motion and, if appropriate, sets a briefing schedule. More generally, no dispositive motion may be filed until counsel confer on its merits and enough discovery is done for the movant to represent there are no disputed material facts; timing must not disrupt the case schedule or trial date.

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Motions and briefing (trap): No reply briefs without prior authorization. LR 7.1 deadlines and page limits otherwise apply. Briefs must be double-spaced (except block quotes), at least 12-point font including footnotes, with 1-inch margins, as text-searchable PDFs; footnotes are strongly discouraged. Noncompliant briefing will be struck by the Clerk. Every motion, procedural or substantive, must state in the caption whether it is “opposed” or “unopposed,” so counsel must confer before filing any motion. Oral argument is held when helpful, often with questions sent in advance; the judge encourages newer lawyers to argue.

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Courtesy copies (trap): Promptly deliver a bound, tabbed courtesy hard copy of all motion briefing and supporting materials (double-sided encouraged). For depositions, include only the cover page and cited pages with the relevant language highlighted; full transcripts are filed on ECF with the word index. In criminal cases, provide a courtesy hard copy with ECF header of all pretrial filings; in civil trials, of jury instructions and deposition transcripts.

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: Initial disclosures must be exchanged at least 2 weeks before the CMC, and they mean actual documents, not just a list. Absent agreement, no formal discovery before the CMC except on jurisdiction or emergency relief. Plaintiff’s counsel arranges the Rule 26(f) meeting; the jointly signed report is filed at least 3 days before the CMC. The standard track means trial within 15 months of filing. The CMC may be by phone, and party attendance may be excused per the notice; to request telephone participation for hardship, call opposing counsel and chambers (419-213-5675) at least 1 week ahead. At counsel’s request, the judge holds a combined settlement and case management conference, which requires counsel and representatives with full authority (in person or remotely unless excused). docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Discovery: Discovery must be proportional, and depositions are staged under the 2015 amendments. Expert depositions require prior court approval. LR 37.1 governs. Counsel may agree to extend discovery deadlines without court approval if the trial date is unaffected. A set trial month or date moves only for good cause, “really good cause.”

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Settlement conferences: Encouraged; parties and counsel (or a representative with full authority) must appear in person. Submit a confidential ex parte settlement statement to chambers before the conference: 2 days before per the judge’s page, 3 days before per the CMC order form. For referrals to a magistrate judge, email that judge’s statement 3 days ahead and report to Judge Zouhary’s chambers right after the conference.

docs.t: Judge Jack Zouhary (N.D. Ohio) — Pretrial motions and filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Civil motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Civil motions and briefing (trap): On a Rule 12 motion to dismiss or for judgment on the pleadings, the courtroom deputy issues an order giving plaintiff one month to oppose and defendant two weeks to reply. Dispositive motions generally get one month for opposition and two weeks for reply; with a counter-motion, one month for the combined response and two weeks for the counter-movant’s reply. Page limits in the Local Rules are preferred but not mandatory; no prior leave is needed to exceed them when the issues warrant. Put document-number and page citations in the text, not footnotes. The judge always prefers a reply. If you will not file one, tell the courtroom deputy promptly, or the motion may not be treated as ready for decision. If a motion has been ready for decision more than two months, or you need it expedited, tell the deputy (Tina Damoah, 419-2

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment, Daubert, and certification
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment, Daubert, and certification: Summary judgment motions are usually due one month after all discovery closes, unless the parties want expert discovery held pending the motion. Brief any Daubert issues before filing for summary judgment; the judge will decide them promptly first. If a motion turns on an unresolved, dispositive question of Ohio (or another state’s) law, ask the court to consider certification to that state’s supreme court before briefing.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Reconsideration (trap)
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Reconsideration (trap): Motions for reconsideration are strongly disfavored. A motion that merely challenges the court’s reasoning or has no plausible justification draws sanctions of the greater of $2,000 or the prevailing party’s actual fees and costs.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes: Discovery may start before the CMC by agreement, and counsel may agree to exceed the federal and local discovery limits without a motion for leave. After a good-faith conference (need not be in person), notify chambers, preferably by email, with a brief description; the judge personally handles discovery disputes, including during depositions. No privilege log unless ordered; disputed documents under 40 pages may be submitted under seal at least 3 business days before the conference. Do not end a deposition without first contacting chambers. No speaking objections, rudeness, or profanity; resolve email delays by phone.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — CMC, TROs, and filing
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. CMC, TROs, and filing: The CMC is usually set earlier than the Local Rules timetable. Ideally meet and confer and file a Report of the Parties’ Planning Meeting a week before. A TRO applicant must make all reasonable efforts to identify defense counsel and send them the complaint, motion, and brief, unless notice would jeopardize plaintiff’s interests. Everything must be filed text searchable, including depositions and critical exhibits. Pro hac vice admission may be moved orally at the CMC or another pretrial conference if no one objects.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Settlement conferences (trap): Usually by Zoom, hosted by chambers. Lead trial counsel must participate, and entity representatives need full authority, meaning authority to settle up to the opposing party’s final pre-conference demand. Referral to Magistrate Judge Clay or others is available on request. Plaintiff’s good-faith demand is due 3 weeks before; defendant’s offer 2 weeks before; each side files an ex parte narrative settlement statement 1 week before (strengths and weaknesses of each side, last demand/offer, and what the client will accept or pay). The judge routinely asks parties to agree to binding, non-appealable resolution by the judge of post-settlement disputes and to retained jurisdiction.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances and pretrial deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Continuances and pretrial deadlines (trap): The trial date is firm; counsel may not stipulate to move it or make other substantive schedule changes. Modest changes that do not disrupt filing deadlines or trial may be made with advance notice to the courtroom deputy. Motions in limine 2 weeks before trial, oppositions 1 week before. Witness lists (in calling order) and marked exhibits exchanged 1 week before trial; plaintiff uses numbers, defendant letters, one per exhibit. Technology or special exhibit needs to the deputy 2 weeks before trial. Proposed jury instructions (substantive only, with sources) and special verdicts are due 1 week before trial after the parties confer. Preference: Sixth Circuit pattern, then Devitt & Blackmar, then Sand; Ohio law from Ohio Jury Instructions. Trial briefs only if requested.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial: Trials run Tuesday through Friday, with voir dire usually the Monday afternoon before. Be available at 8:15 a.m.; trial runs to 4:30 or 5 p.m. At day’s end, tell the court and opposing counsel the next day’s witnesses, exhibits, and expected length, and raise objections then. A magistrate judge may conduct voir dire on consent; counsel participate. Cause challenges at sidebar immediately after the juror’s questioning; peremptories alternate outside the jury’s presence. Twelve jurors usually deliberate. Before each witness, briefly summarize the testimony. Objections are brief with the rule cited; no speaking objections, and argument is at sidebar. Show exhibits to opposing counsel before displaying them. Jurors may ask screened questions if all counsel agree.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases: Surety bonds are strongly disfavored; propose alternatives such as third-party custody, property bonds, or location monitoring. No appraisal or financial documentation is needed to post property. Rule 16, Jencks, and Brady discovery motions are usually unnecessary. For motions needing an evidentiary hearing (e.g., suppression), file a brief statement of grounds; legal briefing follows the hearing. Other motions must be fully briefed; counsel may exceed Local Rule page limits. Sentencing memoranda are due 10 days before sentencing, filed under seal, with typewritten (not handwritten) attachments. The judge considers a blanket refusal to let the defendant meet with Probation inappropriate. No post-trial contact with jurors outside the courthouse without court approval.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: The CMC is held in Chambers 318, 1716 Spielbusch Avenue, Toledo. Parties need not attend unless ordered. Local counsel must attend in person or arrange telephone participation by calling chambers (419-213-5570); out-of-town counsel may arrange to participate by phone. If settlement talks would help at the CMC, tell chambers so extra time can be set aside and party attendance secured. Counsel should be ready to discuss claims and defenses in detail.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Rule 26(f) report and early discovery
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Rule 26(f) report and early discovery: Plaintiff’s counsel arranges the Rule 26(f) meeting; a jointly signed report substantially in the court’s form is due at least 3 days before the CMC. The form asks for the recommended track, ADR suitability, magistrate-judge consent, e-discovery issues (with a reminder of the Appendix K default standard), and proposed amendment, expert, discovery, and dispositive-motion dates. All Rule 26(a) disclosures apply, on a date agreed by counsel or set at the CMC. Absent agreement, no formal discovery before the CMC except as needed for jurisdictional challenges or emergency, temporary, or preliminary relief. Local Rule 30.1 governs deposition conduct.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes (trap): No motion to compel, for a protective order, or for sanctions may be filed unless the parties have tried in good faith to resolve the dispute and then contacted the court by phone or email to request judicial resolution. Local Civil Rule 37.1 governs. The standard CMC order provides that inadvertent disclosure of privileged or work-product material does not waive protection in this or any other proceeding (Evidence Rule 502(d)).

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Filing discovery
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Filing discovery: Without leave, discovery material is not filed except as needed to support dispositive motions. Filed depositions must include the Word Index.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Settlement conferences (trap): Settlement conferences are held before Judge Knepp in Chambers 318. Parties and lead trial counsel must appear; a person with ultimate settlement authority must be personally present, and an insurer that will decide settlement must send a representative in person with full authority. Failing to bring the right people can bring fees, costs, or other sanctions. The conference usually starts with opening presentations, then joint discussion and private caucuses. Statements made are not to be used in discovery and are inadmissible at trial. Counsel must give clients a copy of the order and review it with them beforehand.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement exchanges and statements (trap)
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Settlement exchanges and statements (trap): Plaintiff sends a written itemized damages demand with a brief explanation 14 days before the conference; defendant responds with a written offer 7 days before. If no settlement results, plaintiff’s counsel emails the settlement positions to chambers 3 days before the conference. Each party emails a confidential settlement statement to Knepp_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov 3 days before the conference (not filed): facts, legal analysis, strengths and weaknesses, settlement position and latest proposal, and efforts to date, with critical documents not already in the file.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Attendance at every proceeding (trap)
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Attendance at every proceeding (trap): The judge’s page states that counsel of record, all parties, and a representative with settlement authority must attend every scheduled proceeding. For the case management conference, status conference, and final pretrial, “party” means the named individual or, for an entity, the person most familiar with the facts, not in-house counsel or someone who merely has settlement authority. “Final authority” means the ability to settle without further consultation up to the plaintiff’s prayer for relief (unlimited if no prayer is stated or equitable relief is sought). If that representative cannot attend in person, file a motion showing good cause more than 48 hours before the conference.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Filing format (trap)
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Motions, memoranda, and all other documents must use only 12-point text.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: Report directly to Chambers 18A. The agenda follows Local Rule 16.3(b)(2). Discovery must start before the Rule 26(f) conference.
