docs.x: Judge Michael H. Watson, S.D. Ohio. Extensions and continuances: Every extension request, including for filing deadlines, must be a docketed written motion stating the grounds and whether opposing counsel consents; you may call chambers to say it has been filed. To continue a hearing or conference, first confer and propose agreed dates; if the reason is a conflicting proceeding, give its caption, case number, and judge. If no agreement, say so. Criminal: a motion to continue a hearing or trial must be filed at least 7 days before the trial date, address the § 3161(h)(8)(B) factors, and state whether opposing counsel and the defendant consent.

docs.x: Judge Michael H. Watson, S.D. Ohio. Sealing, depositions, and other motions: Sealing requires leave by docketed motion meeting the Sixth Circuit’s strict standard. In criminal cases, also email the motion and the document for in camera review to chambers. If you cite a deposition in a civil motion, file the entire deposition; move for leave to file a redacted version with a sealed complete copy if needed. Motions to strike are disfavored unless aimed at a pleading under Rule 12(f). After filing a TRO motion, counsel must contact chambers to request an informal scheduling conference.

docs.x: Judge Michael H. Watson, S.D. Ohio. Trial practice and conduct (trap): Trials run Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; civil trials may be preempted by the criminal docket. Counsel receive the juror list the Friday afternoon before trial and refer to jurors by number only. Re-cross is permitted only rarely. Object by standing and stating “objection” and the grounds; argue only at sidebar. Only the attorney examining the witness, or giving the opening or closing, may object, and objections during openings and closings are highly disfavored. Stay within one arm’s length of the podium for openings, closings, and examinations. A charge conference before closings sets their length. If a civil case settles after 12:00 p.m. on the business day before trial, the court may assess jury-summoning costs against either or both parties.

docs.x: Judge Michael H. Watson, S.D. Ohio. Criminal practice: A criminal writ application must be hand-delivered to chambers after calling to confirm the judge is available. The government must make Rule 16(a) disclosures within 10 days of the defendant’s request and Rule 16(a)(1)(G) expert disclosures at least 30 days before the final pretrial conference. Each party emails expert reports to the court when disclosed. The government tracks Speedy Trial compliance. Sentencing memoranda are due at least 5 days before sentencing, or the hearing may be reset. The court may continue a sentencing until a pending appellate decision on a dispositive issue; object by written motion with authority.

docs.x: Judge Michael J. Newman, S.D. Ohio. AI ban (trap): No attorney or pro se party may use artificial intelligence in preparing any filing, civil or criminal. Violations can draw sanctions including striking the filing, economic sanctions or contempt, and dismissal. The ban does not reach legal search engines (Westlaw, LexisNexis), internet search engines (Google, Bing), or Microsoft Suite products such as Word. Everyone must immediately tell the court if they discover AI use in any document filed in their case or an opponent’s.

docs.x: Judge Jeff Brown, S.D. Tex.. Discovery disputes (trap): After a serious attempt to resolve the dispute, file a joint letter of no more than 2 pages outlining the dispute, each side’s position, and the efforts to resolve it. The court typically then holds a Zoom conference. No motion to compel may be filed until this procedure is exhausted. The Rule 26(f) meeting must be held in person, by phone, or by video; email meetings are not allowed.

docs.t: Judge Jeff Brown (S.D. Tex.) — Scheduling, continuances, and appearances
docs.x: Judge Jeff Brown, S.D. Tex.. Scheduling, continuances, and appearances: Judge Edison holds the Rule 16 conference and issues the docket-control order; at least one attorney for each represented party must attend. The joint discovery/case management plan (posted form) is due at least 10 days before the conference and must certify, with dates, that disclosures of interested parties have already been filed. Parties may agree to extend discovery and expert deadlines without approval if the dispositive-motion deadline and docket call are unaffected; changing those requires a motion, and agreed continuance motions don’t bind the court. Vacation requests made well in advance are respected. In-person attendance is preferred. Some hearings and conferences are by phone or Zoom; out-of-town counsel may ask the case manager to appear remotely. A TRO, preliminary injunction, or other emergency filing

docs.t: Judge Jeff Brown (S.D. Tex.) — Amended pleadings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeff Brown, S.D. Tex.. Amended pleadings (trap): Amended pleadings must reproduce the entire pleading, with no incorporation by reference without leave. A motion or stipulation to amend must attach a redline showing every change (strikethrough for deletions, underlining for additions); once leave is granted, file and serve the clean version within 14 days of the order. Under the docket-control order form, pleadings may be amended without leave until the amendment deadline; after that, a motion showing good cause under Rule 16(b)(4) is required. In removed cases, adding new parties always requires a motion for leave.

docs.t: Judge Jeff Brown (S.D. Tex.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeff Brown, S.D. Tex.. Pretrial (trap): No joint pretrial order. At least 24 hours before docket call (9:30 a.m.), each party separately files its exhibit list, witness list, proposed voir dire, proposed jury instructions, motions in limine, and deposition designations and objections, and delivers 2 tabbed binders of those filings and 2 tabbed binders of its exhibits. Exchange proposed motions in limine, exhibit lists, and deposition designations at least 1 week before docket call, and confer to narrow the issues. Docket call is the final pretrial conference; the case is set for trial on a date certain within the next 60 days. Pretrial authenticity and admissibility objections follow Local Rules 44 and 46, and Rule 11 applies to authenticity objections. The court tries to rule on objections and admit as many exhibits as possible before trial.

docs.t: Judge Jeff Brown (S.D. Tex.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Jeff Brown, S.D. Tex.. Trial: The court conducts a preliminary voir dire, and each side may briefly examine the panel if proposed questions were properly submitted. The parties may agree to use a deposition even if the witness is available. Don’t “tender” an expert to the court for recognition of expertise; all such tenders are refused. Bench trials follow the same pretrial filings; the parties must file proposed findings and conclusions, and the court may allow post-trial briefs instead of closings or require findings before trial.

docs.t: Judge Jeff Brown (S.D. Tex.) — Settlement and special matters
docs.x: Judge Jeff Brown, S.D. Tex.. Settlement and special matters: Call the case manager when settlement is contemplated so pending motions can be held, and report settlement immediately. Every settlement announcement draws a conditional dismissal, without prejudice to reinstatement within 60 days. A minor plaintiff’s settlement with a parent conflict requires a joint motion to appoint a guardian ad litem. Social security appeals must be opened using only the claimant’s initials in the last-name field. Initial ex parte admiralty motions go to Judge Edison, with Word proposed orders emailed to Judge Edison’s case manager. In criminal cases, motions to suppress must be filed before the pretrial conference unless ordered otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Pre-motion conference required (trap)
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Pre-motion conference required (trap): Before filing any motion, brief, or materials on a discovery dispute or other pretrial dispute (including requests to extend or modify deadlines), arrange a conference with the court by emailing or faxing the case manager, Glenda Hassan (Glenda_Hassan@txs.uscourts.gov; fax 713-250-5213), and opposing counsel. The court usually schedules it within a few days and may hold it by Zoom or phone. The requesting party submits a 1–2 page letter, copied to all counsel and unrepresented parties, that serves as an agenda only, with no case law or argument. Opponents respond the same way, with the same limits, before the conference. Each letter must state that counsel conferred in good faith and couldn’t agree, or why they couldn’t confer. The court tries to resolve the issues at the conference without formal motions; if brief

docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Discovery objections (trap)
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Discovery objections (trap): Boilerplate objections are prohibited for every form of discovery. No “Preamble” or “General Objections” section, and no objections “to the extent that” a request is vague, overbroad, or burdensome; each objection must be specific and tied to a particular request. A response “subject to” objections must say whether it is complete and, if anything is withheld because of the objections, give enough information about what was withheld to allow further inquiry. A partial production must state whether and when more will be produced. Requests must meet Rule 26(b)(1) relevance and proportionality; parties may not over-ask, or object and withhold needed material, for strategic or tactical reasons.

docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Initial conference and Rule 26(f) plan
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Initial conference and Rule 26(f) plan: Counsel with knowledge of the case and authority on substantive and scheduling matters must attend both the Rule 26(f) meeting and the Rule 16 conference. To attend the Rule 16 conference by phone or Zoom, email the case manager at least 2 business days before; an in-person conference may be required if substantive issues will be addressed. Be prepared to address pending motions. File one joint Discovery/Case Management Plan and proposed Scheduling and Docket Control Order, signed by all counsel and unrepresented parties, at least 14 days before the Rule 16 conference. Plaintiff’s counsel files them (or represented parties’ counsel if the plaintiff is pro se), and disagreements must be set out clearly. Restate each instruction in the form before answering. docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Case-type initial discovery protocols (trap)
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Case-type initial discovery protocols (trap): In FLSA cases not pleaded as collective actions, the parties must exchange the protocol’s listed documents and information within 30 days after the defendant’s responsive pleading or motion. In first-party property insurance cases arising from disasters, the deadline is 45 days, and the parties must meet and confer on production format within 14 days after the order. In residential mortgage default or foreclosure cases where a borrower is a party, it is 30 days after the earlier of a responsive pleading or motion or a notice of removal. The protocols replace Rule 26(a)(1) initial disclosures for those claims. The exchanges are not subject to objection except privilege or work product (and, in FLSA cases, Rule 26(b)(2)(B)); a partial answer must state why it is incomplete. Each protocol comes with an interim

docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Motions and briefs
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Motions and briefs: Dispositive and other motions generally follow the Local Rules’ written motion practice and are considered after the submission date. Oral argument must be requested in writing with an explanation of why it would help. Briefs are limited to 25 pages without leave. Every brief must include a statement of the nature and stage of the proceeding, the issues and standard of review for each with authority, informative headings, and a short conclusion stating the precise relief; briefs with more than 10 pages of argument also need tables of contents and authorities and a summary of argument. Put cited affidavits and discovery in an appendix; hyperlinks to cited cases are encouraged. Parties may agree to extend a motion submission date without leave unless that breaches a court-ordered deadline; notify the case manager in writing immediately

docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Emergencies, continuances, and contact
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Emergencies, continuances, and contact: File TRO and other emergency applications and email a copy to the case manager, stating whether the other side has been contacted and when all parties can attend a conference. Ex parte TROs are considered only if Rule 65(b) is met. Motions to extend deadlines are generally not emergencies. Joint motions for continuance are not binding. Vacation requests made well ahead of a setting will be respected, but a trial generally won’t be continued for an unavailable witness; be ready to use a deposition or stipulation. Unless counsel has actually begun trial elsewhere, other trial settings won’t delay a case set for trial. Direct inquiries to the case manager, in writing when time permits, never to the judge’s secretary or law clerks. Don’t argue substantive issues in letters, which may be docketed. docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Joint pretrial order and docket call (trap): Plaintiff must ensure the complete joint pretrial order, signed by all counsel and unrepresented parties, is filed on time; late filing can lead to dismissal or other sanctions. Jury trials: one joint proposed charge with each instruction, definition, and question numbered on a separate page with authority, disputed items in bold, italics, or underlining and labeled by requesting party, also submitted on a Word-compatible CD, plus a memorandum of law. Bench trials: proposed findings and conclusions and a memorandum of law. docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Exhibits and depositions at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Exhibits and depositions at trial (trap): Mark exhibits with party name, case number, and exhibit number and exchange them before trial. Give written notice within 7 days after an exhibit is identified if you require authentication, or authenticity may be deemed admitted. Listed exhibits are admitted unless written objections with authority are filed at least 7 days before trial. Provide the court a notebook of your exhibits, and give the case manager 2 copies of exhibits before or during trial as well as filing them on CM/ECF. Don’t pass exhibits to the jury without advance permission. Designate deposition excerpts by page and line in the joint pretrial order; objections with authority are due at least 7 days before trial. Give the case manager a copy of any deposition to be used, edit videotapes to reflect rulings, and in bench trials offer the whole

docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Trial days and courtroom
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Trial days and courtroom: Court normally runs 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with about a 45-minute lunch; counsel should arrive earlier and stay later than the jury. Test any technology every morning before trial, and arrange extra equipment and after-hours courtroom access with the case manager and security in advance. The court conducts preliminary voir dire, then each side may examine the panel. Counsel may question from counsel table or a lectern. The court generally won’t recess for a missing witness unless the witness was subpoenaed and failed to appear. Counsel table seating is first-come, first-served on the first day; use only the front doors. No contact with jurors after discharge except as the court permits.

docs.t: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal (S.D. Tex.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Lee H. Rosenthal, S.D. Tex.. Settlement: Promptly notify the case manager of any settlement of a case set for conference, hearing, or trial, and file closing papers within 30 days of the announcement. If a minor plaintiff’s case settles, counsel jointly move for a guardian ad litem if needed (each side proposes 3 names if they can’t agree) and request a settlement conference by letter to the case manager.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ganjei (S.D. Tex.) — AI certification (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ganjei, S.D. Tex.. AI certification (trap): Every motion, response, and reply must end with a separate-page certification (like a certificate of service) stating whether AI was used at any point in research, outlining, drafting, or editing, which program or model, and that lead counsel verified all facts and citations under Rule 11. A “no AI” certification is still required. Omitting the certification or including “hallucinated” facts or authority can lead to striking the brief and sanctions against the certifying attorney. The rule applies to pro se litigants too.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ganjei (S.D. Tex.) — Briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ganjei, S.D. Tex.. Briefing (trap): Word limits, not pages: motions and responses 5,000 words (about 25 pages), replies 2,000 words (about 10), with a word-count certificate after the signature block. Limits exclude caption, tables, signature, and certificates, and are rarely extended. No sur-replies without permission. Fonts: Times New Roman 13 or larger, or Book Antiqua or Century Schoolbook 12 or larger; 1-inch margins; double-spaced. No separate memorandum of law; file a single motion. Every motion needs the nature and stage of the proceeding, facts, issues, the standard of review for each issue with authority, argument, and a short conclusion on the precise relief, under headings. docs.t: Judge Nicholas Ganjei (S.D. Tex.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas Ganjei, S.D. Tex.. Motions (trap): Confer in good faith on all requests for relief, including dispositive motions; motions without a certificate of conference may be struck. Before a Rule 12(b)(6) or 12(c) motion, identify the defects to the opponent and confer, and say so in the certificate. Responses are due 21 days after the motion and replies 10 days after the response; opposed motions are considered when briefing closes.
